data.line_text: Of all the Gifts Thy love bestows,
E'en heav'n itself no richer knows
Faith, too, that trusts the blood through grace,
From that same love we gain;
Else, sweetly as it suits our case,
The gift had been in vain.
We praise Thee, and would praise Thee more;
To Thee our all we owe;
The precious Saviour, and the power
Father, 'twas Thy love that knew us
That same love to Jesus drew us
Now that changeless love enfolds us,
All its wealth on us bestows;
While its power unchanging holds us
As Head, O God, exalted Thou,
Riches and glory are of Thee;
Thou rulest over all in love,
And in that love Thy sons are free.
Now in Thy hand is power and might,
Thy Spirit makes all great and strong;
So we as strengthened thus for Thee,
Now praise Thy glorious name in song.
Thy glorious Name! A hush divine
Falls on our spirits as we sing.
God - Father, Son and Holy Ghost -
To Thee our worship now we bring.
Thine is the love, Lord, that draws us together,
Guiding our steps from the wilderness ways;
Soon face to face we'll adore Thee for ever,
Now our glad hearts would be filled with Thy praise.
While for this moment, O Lord, we have waited,
Oft has the Comforter spoken of Thee;
Now with love's treasure our spirits are freighted,
Bowed at Thy feet, and the fragrance set free.
For us, Lord Jesus, thyself Thou hast given;
Suff'rings unfathomed for us hast thou known;
Now, in accord with the homage of heaven,
Rises a song from the hearts of Thine own.
Jesus, Lord Jesus, we love and adore Thee;
Glorious Thy Name, all our praises above;
Peerless Thy beauty, we wait now before Thee,
Moved are our hearts in response to Thy love.
Father of glory, Thine is now the praise,
As in the light of heav'n's unclouded rays
The glory of a past eternal plan,
The glory of a love ere time began,
We glory in the thought that Thou wast there
Before there was a creature formed to share
And worship at the mighty, sovereign thought,
That we as sons should with Thy Son be brought
To fill Thy heart this counsel was conceived;
By Him the working out was all achieved,
What part have we as brought into this place,
Father, we worship Thee as we discern
That thou hast been enriched through love's return
For, added to the riches that were then,
Thou hast secured vast myriads of men
Jesus! How much Thy Name unfolds
That God as Man could show;
Thus only could we fully trace
Jesus - it speaks a life of love,
Jesus, the One who knew not sin,
Made sin to make us just;
Thou gav'st Thyself our love to win,
The mention of Thy Name doth bow
The chiefest of ten thousand Thou,
Whose love has set us free.
Hark! happy saints! loud lift your voice,
Tell to the world how we rejoice -
There live our Head with glory crowned;
And we as for His kingdom bound,
For of Thee are all things
All hail the power of Jesus' Name!
With one accord His praise proclaim,
And crown Him Lord of all.
Ye saints redeemed from Adam's race,
Hail Him who saves you by His grace,
And crown Him Lord of all.
Tell forth the only Name that's giv'n
On which we now may call,
The Name adored by hosts in heav'n,
And crown Him Lord of all.
In glory all the ransomed throng
Soon at His feet shall fall;
Join in the blest eternal song,
And crown Him Lord of all.
Our God and Father, may our souls repose
In the deep sense of Thine unfailing love!
Kept by thy peace, in Him who died and rose,
Till we are gathered to Thy rest above.
Thou art the blest incarnate Word,
God manifest, God seen and heard,
The Lamb of God, exalted Lord,
Worthy art Thou to be adored!
With Thee before the Father's face,
Yet loving Thee, on whom His love
Our hearts are led to Him above,
And we with Thee are blest.
The Father's Name Thou hast declared,
the Father's love with Thee is shared.
Of the vast universe of bliss
Th'eternal theme of praise is this,
Fills all that scene, where God alone
In His own rest is fully known.
How all things shine in light divine
For those who've seen His face.
For us that place has won;
In Him we stand, a heav'nly band,
Our hearts let in its rays;
And heav'nly light makes all things bright,
Such here on earth we are,
Our place on high, God's self so nigh,
Through scenes of strife and desert life
We tread in peace our way.
Our rest's above, in perfect love
We'll see His face in that blest place,
Man meted to the sinless One
Laid down His life, and e'en the tomb's
The darkness sought His woes to hide;
He lives to die no more,
Thence, where the blood is seen alway,
Is flowing o'er the barren place
No tongue but shall confess Him then,
Worthy that all to Him should bow,
Wake at once the echoing chord.
Praise the Lamb! - the chorus waking,
Loud and far, each tongue partaking,
All the mind in heav'n is one.
Crowned with light and joy unfading,
Hail Him as the great "I AM".
Hark! still louder swells the singing,
As the notes are heard again;
Lord, on the throne Thy love's the same
As once upon Thy cross of shame;
In lowliness Thou cam'st to die,
Thou livest now for us on high.
We see Thee there, the Lamb once slain;
Thy loss was our eternal gain;
We see Thee crowned with glory now,
No shade on Thy victorious brow.
But now thine unveiled face we see;
Praise be to God for that blest word,
E'en heav'n, shall pass, but Thou shalt stand;
Changeless through all the changing years.
Blest Victor, Thou, o'er every power malign,
We hail Thee, Lord, in majesty divine,
As in the midst, in all Thy greatness now;
To Thee in worship, with glad hearts, we bow,
Effulgence of God's glory, blessed Lord!
Expression of His substance! Thus adored
By those who are the fruit of love divine,
Supreme art Thou, as all Thy glories shine!
May the grace of Christ our Saviour,
Thus may we abide in union
With each other and the Lord,
Joys which earth can ne'er afford.
Unseen, yet known to us through grace,
We see our Saviour face to face:
His wondrous love, well known through Thee,
Has set our longing spirits free.
We bow and own Thy sovereign will,
Which prompted first our hearts to yield;
Blest impulse giv'n when born anew
By power divine, which Thou didst wield;
That power springs up in life by Thee,
As with us, blessed Spirit, now,
Thou dost reveal the depths of love
Which eye nor ear hath seen nor heard,
The things prepared by God above.
In glad response we sing to Thee;
For ever with Thee, at Thy coming again;
We'll live in Thy grace, Lord,
When finished our race, at Thy coming again.
The traits of that face. Lord,
With joy we shall trace at Thy coming again;
Our sorrow be o'er at Thy coming again.
We'll sit on Thy throne, Lord,
Of all to be known at Thy coming again.
When all is gone by, at Thy coming again.
The gulf between all else and Thee -
Filling with joy all heav'n around!
Thy counsel, ere the world began;
O God, of all Thy wondrous plan,
For the Father and the Son
Unto Thee, as God, we bow;
How bright, there above, is the mercy of God!
And void of all guilt, and clear of all sin,
Are my conscience and heart, through my Saviour's blood:
Not a cloud above - not a spot within.
Christ died! then I'm clean: not a spot within.
God's mercy and love! not a cloud above.
'Tis the Spirit, through faith, thus triumphs o'er sin:
Not a cloud above - not a spot within.
How good is the God we adore,
Whose love is as great as His power,
And knows neither measure nor end.
'Tis Jesus, the First and the Last,
Whose Spirit shall guide us safe home;
We'll praise Him for all that is past,
And trust Him for all that's to come.
He won the meed and crown;
Trod all our foes beneath His feet,
Bowed to the grave, destroyed it so,
Who lived, who died, who lives again
Father, Thy name our souls would bless,
Lift up our hearts in righteousness
Sweet is the confidence Thou giv'st,
Our hearts resort to where Thou liv'st
There in the purpose of Thy love
As sons with Him who is above,
Absent as yet, we rest in hope,
Waiting for Him who takes us up
O Holy Father, keep us here
In that blest Name of love,
Father, thy love our portion is,
As sons, like Christ, with Thee;
O who can tell of love like this,
His Father Thou, and ours through grace,
Blest in the brightness of Thy face,
But brighter joy our spirits trace
To those who with Thy Son shall share
Father, Thy love, the source of all,
Shines on us now without recall,
We joy in Thee, Thy holy love
Like Thine own Son, with Him above,
O God, we rejoice in Thy greatness and might.
To Thee be the glory! To Thee every right!
Thy Name is Almighty, Thy way is unknown,
Thy love is unmeasured, Thy wisdom we own.
Though empires should crumble, though nations should fall,
Thy presence is with us - Thine arm ruleth all.
Thy grace will sustain us the whole journey through,
As waiting upon Thee our strength we renew.
Thou didst suffer, Lord, to save us,
Nigh to God Thine own to bring.
Hail! once lowly Man of sorrows,
Bearer of our grief and shame;
Graced in Thee by God's own favour,
Life we have in Thy blest Name.
There in heav'n our hearts accord Thee
Now for us in patience waiting,
With Thy loved ones all to share:
Soon we shall, as come to glory,
Of Thy dying love so great.
Love that none below can tell.
In the bread we break Thou speakest
Of Thy body giv'n for us:
In His service day by day;
Nothing but His will Thy measure
Lord, we drink the cup of blessing,
Thus as one our love confessing
For Thyself, blest Son of God.
A while, yes, a very short while now of waiting,
And then will our Lord come to call us away;
With prayer and with fasting then let us be watching,
For - well do we know it - He will not delay.
With voice of archangel, from heaven descending,
With great acclamation and trumpet of God,
To us us shall the One whom our hearts are awaiting,
That very same Jesus, appear in the cloud.
We know that the saints who in Christ have been sleeping,
By God's mighty power from sleep shall awake;
We shall not before them be caught up to heaven,
But Christ all His loved ones together shall take.
Revealed to our sight in Thy glorious descending,
Lord Jesus, Thou shalt to Thy lovers appear;
And then shalt Thou take us to heaven rejoicing,
Eternally with Thee Thy glories to share.
Our hearts unite to render Thee
To grieve Thee not, on Thee depend,
Thus would we seek to move,
By grace and strength which Thou dost give,
Come, Prince of Peace, for now
The Saviour, Jesus, who is He?
The mighty God, a Man become!
A Saviour now for such as we,
To bring to God the wand'rers home.
His blood was shed upon the tree,
To cleanse from sin and make us free.
In this poor world thou'lt find no rest;
Then from Thy fruitless strivings cease!
Thou'lt find it in the Saviour blest,
There shall Thy soul have perfect peace.
The Saviour, Jesus, who is He?
The One who gave Himself for me!
O God of love, how measureless
Thy thoughts to us are shown!
More precious they than tongue can tell,
We can but bless Thee for the light
To those Thy love has sealed.
We boast in Thee, Thou source of good,
Our heart are filled with holy joy,
And, Father, Son and Spirit now
The heav'ns, which now conceal Him
He shall come down like showers
And joy and hope, like flowers,
Spring up where He doth pass;
Kings shall fall down before Him
Or dove's light wing can soar.
We are graced in God's own Son;
Fill the vision of our soul,
This - the Spirit's realm of glory -
Now to Thee, O God, we bow.
"All things new," our eyes look upward,
Old things now have passed away;
When Thou dost behold in heaven
And on earth the things that are,
It is said, Thyself Thou humblest -
Who to Thee hath given counsel?
Who Thy mind hath ever known?
Of the things that are Thine own.
But the glory of Thy greatness
To the feelings of Thy heart.
Thou art now in Christ revealed.
Lord Jesus, in Thee we're rejoicing,
For Thou hast come near to us now,
God's will in its vastness Thou lovedst
And camest as Man it to do,
Thy life was laid down in rare fragrance,
That Thou mightest take it anew.
And now Thou art there, the Beginning
Of all that shall be for God's rest,
And we, Lord, are with Thee as of Thee,
Embraced in a nearness most blest.
The Holy One, a Victim, dies -
The Lamb of God, a Sacrifice;
God's love in fulness there made known
When Jesus did for sins atone.
O solemn hour! O hour alone,
When God the Father's only Son,
As Man for sinners to atone,
The Lord of life Himself has died!
Worthy of death, O God, we were,
In grace Thy spotless Lamb did bear,
Himself, our sins while hanging there;
With Him, our Surety, we have died,
When He for us was crucified.
Quickened with Him in life divine,
Raised with Him from the dead:
His own (and all His own are Thine)
Shall with Him in His glories shine,
We, who were worthy but to die,
Are by His precious blood made nigh.
Thou hast loved us, Thou hast bought us,
Hearts and voices blend in singing,
Thine the cost and Thine the suff'ring,
Thine the fruit now of the travail
O wondrous thought, that Thou, blest Lord, shouldst have
An object suited to Thy manhood's state!
A helpmate, like Thee, builded by Thy God,
To Thee united - mystery how great!
Lord Jesus, true responses now we give
To Thee, whose deep affections stir our heart;
Soon we shall share Thy headship by Thy side,
But now in holy union have our part.
Jesus, our Saviour, we gladly adore Thee,
Joyfully Thee as our Lord do we own;
Blest in Thy presence we worship before Thee,
Thou who art worthy to sit on the throne.
How hast Thou triumphed, and triumphed with glory!
Battled death's forces, rolled back every wave!
Can we refrain then from telling the story,
How Thou art Victor o'er death and the grave?
"Lord, what is man?" we would break forth exclaiming;
Jesus, the crowned One, the Lamb that was slain!
Joyful we own Thee, Thy praises proclaiming;
Death Thou hast vanquished by rising again.
"Lord, what is man?" Yes, with deep adoration,
Gladly prolong we this wonderful theme;
Jesus, divine One, Thou Head of creation,
Head of Thy church and o'er all things supreme!
Lord Jesus Christ, in all Thy grace,
God's glory radiant in Thy face,
Who once didst take the sinner's place -
To Thee, my Lord, I come.
Now where Thou art, God's blessed Son,
In heights of glory Thou hast won
In virtue of Thy work well done -
To Thee, my Lord, I come.
To know Thee there in all Thy love,
Who once in death that love didst prove -
To Thee, my Lord, I come.
Just as Thou art in glory bright,
Centre of heaven's courts of light,
Worthy of honour, power and might -
To Thee, my Lord, I come.
Lord, from myself I gladly turn,
In Thee God's grace and love to learn;
For Thou wilt not the weakest spurn!
To Thee, my Lord, I come.
Our God and Father, we would now proclaim
With sacred joy the wonders of Thy Name;
Thy perfect love our inmost fear has stilled,
And every heart with peace divine has filled.
The glorious worth of Thine own Son we bring,
And His renown with adoration sing -
Jesus the Christ, who stooped in grace so low,
That we Thy love in all its wealth might know.
Father, our hearts are filled, and Thee we praise -
Thou sovereign fount of joy through endless days!
Now brought to Thee and by Thy Spirit led,
We worship Thee through Christ, our blessed Head.
Peace He offers thee, and pardon.
Wilt thou now to Him belong?
Is Thy heart oppressed with sorrow
In the world where death is rife?
One who knows and understands thee,
Bids thee come - in Him is life.
He would turn Thee from sin's pleasures,
Where no lasting joy is found;
Grace that would to thee abound.
Ere thy heart commenced its beating,
Or thine eyes beheld the light,
Love divine for men was planning
Even though thy sins condemn thee,
He who knows it died to save thee,
Bore sin's load in all its weight.
Now He lives a Man in heaven,
Waiting now to save and bless thee,
Blest Lord, Thou spakest! 'twas Thy voice
That led our hearts to Thee;
That drew us to that better choice,
Where grace has set us free.
Thou wouldest that we should rejoice,
Enough, that we have heard Thy voice,
And learned Thy love's deep woe -
Thy glory, Lord: this living waste
To us no rest can give;
Our path is on with earnest haste,
Lord, in Thy rest to live.
Our happiness, O Lord, with Thee
Is long laid up in store,
For that blest day when Thee we'll see,
Yes, love divine in Thee we know;
Shall burst upon our ravished view,
Soon shall we see Thee as Thou art,
Thou'lt call us, in our heav'nly part,
Where we shall ever see Thee shine,
Blest Father of glory, we worship,
We bless Thee, Thy Spirit within us
Gives power to these heavenly lays.
We think of the Man in Thy presence,
Set down there, exalted as head;
Once raised by the might of Thy power,
When numbered along with the dead.
We think of the glory that chose us,
The glory of love that redeemed us,
Through Jesus, the Man of Thy choice.
As marked out beforehand for sonship,
We praise now the glory of grace
And bow in Thy presence and worship,
As conscious, in Christ, of our place.
Lord, in Thee we taste the sweetness
Of the Tree of Life above;
For the heav'nly land we love.
Food of heav'nly life to be;
Fresh and ever new are yielded
Fruits of life on that blest Tree.
One itself, the same for ever,
Fruits that now our souls have tasted
While through desert lands we've hasted;
So sweet, so full, so free;
To joy in all its brightness,
Yet sure, if in Thy presence
If clouds have dimmed my sight,
Towards me, as e'er, Thou'rt bright.
O keep my soul, then, Jesus,
And, if I wander, teach me
Soon back to Thee to flee;
May to my soul be known;
And, versed in this Thy goodness,
We sing to Thee, blest Father,
Where now in joy we rest.
Who for Thine own heart's pleasure
Thy sons marked out for glory -
Who else but Thee, O Father,
So bless us with Thy Spirit,
And have us for Thine own?
Soon shall we be for ever
We'll shine in His blest image
We'll sing of God's wonderful gospel,
Christ's Person, His work, and His glory,
We love Him for all He has done.
His Person is ever the Same;
But stooping in grace into manhood
To save us, lost sinners, He came.
His work, praise His Name! He completed
Alone, when He died on the tree;
The judgment of sin was His burden,
He bore it for you and for me.
Ascended at God's own right hand,
Accepted in Him now we stand.
The Father's delight is in Jesus,
And those whom His blood has secured,
The Spirit would keep Him before us,
Through Christ we have present salvation,
From sin and the world would we turn,
And walk here in true separation,
How sweet the name of Jesus sounds
It soothes his sorrows, heals his wounds,
It makes the wounded spirit whole,
Blest Name! the rock on which we build,
Our Lord, our Life, our Way, our End,
Weak is the effort of our heart,
But when we see Thee as Thou art,
We'll praise Thee as we ought.
Till then we would Thy love proclaim
And triumph in Thy blessed Name
Which quells the power of death.
Through waves, through clouds and storms,
We wait His time; so shall the night
And all things serve His might;
His every act pure blessing is,
When He makes bare His arm,
When He His people's cause defends,
Who then shall stay His hand?
With wonder filled, we soon shall see
How wise, how strong His hand!
God sits as sovereign on the throne,
O Lord, how blest our journey,
Though here on earth we roam,
For where Thou now art sitting
Free to look up to heaven,
We have no home but there,
Thy joy with Thee shall share.
No place can fully please us
Where Thou, O Lord, art not;
In Thee, and with Thee, ever
Is found, by grace, our lot.
Where glory lights the courts on high,
Thee, Lord of power and majesty,
O who shall sing that path of worth,
That led up to the throne?
The Corn of Wheat upon this earth
But Thou art risen from the dead,
And we, as one with Thee,
Now sing Thy Name, our Lord, our Head,
Lord Jesus, Thou art waiting yet
Thy blest companion shall be set,
Lord, we are Thine, bought by Thy blood,
Once the poor guilty slaves of sin;
But Thou redeemedst us to God,
And mad'st Thy Spirit dwell within.
Lord, we are Thine, Thy claims we own;
Ourselves to Thee we'd wholly give;
O may our hearts Thyself enthrone,
And let us to Thy glory live!
Here let us each Thy mind display,
In all Thy gracious image shine;
And haste that long expected day
When Thou shalt own that we are Thine.
The heart of God is love;
For Jesus, His own Son, has died
Thy God is not far off;
Thou'lt find Him waiting at Thy side,
Blest source within of living grace
From such a scene of bliss,
And God the father's changeless love
The Father's tender love to know
O God, the great "I AM," we worship Thee
For Thine amazing gift has set men free!
Redemption's work has lifted every load,
Secured a princely people for their God.
We trace Thy counsels deep ere worlds began,
And see Thine own great thoughts in making man.
Thy sovereign will has wrought to set all free,
To bring in life and joy and liberty.
No tear-filled eyes then left to chill the joy
Of new creation's bliss without alloy!
All grief by Thy blest service there removed;
O God of love, Thy love so fully proved!
How choice the notes that rise responsively,
The vast extent of the created sphere
Rejoices, knowing Thou, O God, art near.
Sphere full of love and praise
Our God and Father, Thee we bless,
Extol Thy Name, with joy express
Praise that is due to Thee.
"Greater then all" we know Thy place,
A Father's love holds all in rest,
In Christ in heav'nly places blest,
O Father, how our hearts expand
T'wards Thee, as now in Him we stand,
Whose sight our longing spirit weans
From earth, where yet we roam.
And can we call our home
The rest of God our rest to come
Our hearts' deep longings more than gained
When God His rest shall give.
Shall find, when endless ages roll,
And time shall ne'er grow old.
Once Man of sorrows, full of grace,
That gives us now as heav'nly light
What soon shall be our part!
Lord, as now Thy people gather,
We delight in Thee as Head,
In the world Thou art rejected,
Here we seek to guard Thine interests,
Thou art in our hearts enthroned.
Help us as we now consider
How to care for what is Thine.
May we move as faithful bondmen,
Boldness we would seek for meeting
All we need in skill and wisdom
We would now from Thee derive.
Thou dost trust in Thine assembly
To be faithful to Thy Name,
As a pure and shining witness,
Soon the trump will sound from heaven
Then the vessel Thou hast purchased
Is in Thy Christ made known,
As Man in heav'n is known;
And O what love is beaming
With Thine own Son, our part.
We bless Thee, God and Father,
We share Thy Son's blest place.
He lives a Man before Thee
His God and ours Thou art;
We're His, in joy He brings us
To share His part and place,
To know Thy love and favour,
Thy love that now enfolds us
Can ne'er wax cold or dim;
In Him that love doth centre,
And we are loved in Him.
In Him Thy love and glory
In Him, how near, how blest!
O Lord of glory, who couldst leave
The height supreme in death to lie,
What tongue shall sing, what heart conceive
The love divine that made Thee die?
Bought with a price, for ever Thine,
We bless Thee for Thy stoop divine.
But ris'n, the Firstborn from the dead,
The glorious Man, the living Head,
Thrice worthy Thou our hearts to win!
In Thy blest face all glories shine,
And there we gaze on love divine.
And strike within the answ'ring chord
To love so rich and free.
And cleave to Thy blest side;
To gaze upon Thee where Thou art,
Each day more to Thy stature grow,
The goal to which our hearts aspire,
To meet Thee in the air.
Though vile, you need not fear;
With joy you now may hear,
God's love in Christ we see -
Some guest will be the last,
Then grace no more will say
Sweetly swells the note of praise,
From the chamber where the Saviour
Leads His own the voice to raise.
On the night of His rejection
As the Son of man goes onward
To the cross, to death and tomb.
Softly swells the note of praise;
As to Him the voice we raise.
All our guilt was laid upon Him -
All the waves and billows pouring
O'er His head, He cried, 'Tis done!
Louder swells the note of praise;
Lord, we hail Thee as the Victor
While to Thee the voice we raise.
Thou whom men cast out, rejected,
Yea, Amen! Thou, Lord, art worthy!
Loudly swells the note of praise!
Heav'n and earth shall soon adore Thee,
All to Thee their voices raise.
Thou hast loved us, Thou hast washed us
In Thy blood from every stain;
Raise we then the joyful chorus -
Worthy is the Lamb once slain!
Our God whom we have known,
Rests in the blessing of His own
And countless myriads, owned as His,
More precious still that love to share
As those that love did call.
Like Him, to know that glory beam
Father, Thou lovest! favour all divine,
A cloudless favour rests upon us here;
Thy face shines on us as it still doth shine
On Thy blest Son, whose image we shall bear.
Who, in thy palaces of love,
To us thy joy to tell?
Where God Himself vouchsafes to dwell,
Who shall to us that joy
Tell of that constant sweet employ
No cloud of grief e'er stains;
Unfailing praise each heart doth fill,
Has brought us to that favoured hour
When toil shall all be o'er.
Our souls their strength shall find;
Their life, their joy for evermore,
God and the Lamb shall there
And radiant hosts for ever share
Jesus, our Lord, thy worthiness we sing,
Our sacrifice of praise to Thee we bring,
Thy glories fill our vision with delight,
And heart and voice to honour Thee unite.
Yet wider praise in Zion waits for Thee,
Creation too, in rest and liberty,
Both heav'n and earth shall Thy dominion own,
And every tongue confess Thee Lord alone.
More blessed still - Thine own peculiar joy
Who then shall find their constant blest employ
And with Thee, Lord, Thy glory shall behold,
While love delights its wonders to unfold.
Rise, my soul, thy God directs thee,
Pass thou on, His hand protects thee -
Strength that has the captive freed.
Heav'nly springs shall there restore thee,
God Himself shall mark thy way;
Feeds thee with the mighty's meat;
Egypt's food no more to eat.
Art thou weaned from Egypt's pleasures?
God in secret thee shall keep,
In the desert God will teach thee
What the God that thou hast found -
All His grace shall there abound.
On to Canaan's rest still wending,
E'en thy wants and woes shall bring
Thou shalt taste of mercy's spring.
Though thy way be long and dreary,
Tell how God hath brought thee through.
Love divine thy foot shall bring,
There with shouts of triumph swelling,
Zion's songs in rest to sing;
There no stranger God shall meet thee -
He, who to His rest shall greet thee,
Greets thee with a well known love.
Lord, we love to trace Thy footprints
Ponder o'er Thy path of suffering -
See Thy stoop to Bethlehem's manger,
Hear Thee still the raging wave,
Learn Thy love in all its fulness
At the cross and in the grave.
As we watch that stream of love;
Find its mighty tide still flowing
From Thee now as crowned above.
'Tis a love no heart can fathom,
Which to us Thou dost unfold,
Wondrous theme that ne'er grows old.
O God of grace, our Father,
All praise we give to Thee;
As Thine Thou didst foreknow us
And when was come the moment,
Still leading on Thy loved ones
In each, made meet, yet training,
Of joy and love no tongue can tell,
Yet know that all is mine.
The Lamb is there, my soul,
In love divine diffused through all,
God's treasured store - for ever fed,
His love my soul shall cheer.
Graved on the stone of white.
I'll walk, and in Thy heav'nly light
Which His own hand hath dressed,
My feet press on, where brightest day
Shines forth on all the Rest.
Where all His brightness God displays,
Our eyes on Him we'll rest,
We praise Thee, Lord of glory,
In Thee the Son is seen;
No mind of man conceived it,
Thou art the Son, O Lord.
Thy throne, O God, for ever,
In time they all shall perish,
Thou who dost all things fill!
O Lord, Thy glory we behold,
That glory on the Father's throne
'Tis thence - now Thou art gone on high,
The Spirit brings Thy glory nigh
To those who for Thee wait.
'Tis not for human eye to see,
Nor heart conceive what it may be,
But God, in love, has freely giv'n
All He's prepared for those, in heav'n,
Whom here on earth He seals.
And we our great Forerunner see
Yet not ashamed with such as we,
That world of bliss without alloy,
O Jesus Lord, we love Thee,
For Thou cam'st down from glory
As when on earth Thou drewest
To learn Thy love's sweet story,
So now, O Lord, we gather
O the wondrous joy of dwelling,
All that shone in Christ, once humbled,
By the Spirit's power is strengthened
Every eye on Him to gaze;
Wakes fresh bursts of joyful praise!
Yields of Christ some beauteous ray;
And for Thy delight and pleasure
There Thy love o'er all transcendent
Shall for ever find its rest;
While each heart, its joy outpouring,
In that love is ever blest.
Lord Jesus, gladly do our lips express
Our hearts' deep sense of all Thy worthiness;
Thou risen One, the Holy and the True,
We give Thee now the praise so justly due.
Thou giv'st us, Lord, once more to taste down here
The joy Thy presence brings, its warmth and cheer;
With great delight we 'neath Thy shadow rest;
Thy fruit is sweet to those Thy love has blest.
Thou wast alone, till like the precious grain
In death Thou layest but didst rise again;
And in Thy risen life a countless host
Are "All of one" with Thee, Thy joy and boast.
We bless Thee, Lord, Thou lov'st to take Thy place
Amongst Thine own, who taste Thy boundless grace;
'Tis thus we know Thee as Thou'rt known above
In heav'nly glory - home of perfect love.
There is rest for the weary soul -
There is rest in the Saviour's love;
There is rest in the grace that has made us whole,
And that seeketh out those who rove.
There is rest in the tender love
That has trodden our path below;
That has found us a place in the realms above,
But can now all our sorrows know.
There is rest in the calming grace
That flows out from those realms above;
O what rest in the thought - we shall see His face,
Who has giv'n us to know His love!
There is rest in the midst of grief -
For His grief was the proof of love;
O 'tis sweet in that love now to find relief,
When the sorrows of earth we prove.
There is rest in the Saviour's heart,
Who would never turn grief away:
But has found, in what sin once had made our part,
The domain of His love's display.
There is rest in the blessed yoke,
And in proving no will but His,
While we learn from His path, and the words He spoke,
What that patience of Jesus is!
So where Jesus has gone before
Is the path which we have to tread;
And it leads to the rest where all sorrow's o'er -
To the place where His steps have led.
Through the love of God our Saviour,
Free and changeless is His favour,
Mighty is the power that healed us,
Precious is the grace that sealed us,
Strong the hand stretched forth to shield us:
Ours is such a full salvation,
Faith can sing through days of sorrow,
Or in living, or in dying,
Father, Thy sovereign love has sought
Captives to sin, gone far from Thee;
The work that Thine own Son hath wrought
Has brought us back in peace and free.
And now, as sons before Thy face,
With joyful steps the path we tread,
Which leads us on to that blest place
Prepared for us by Christ our Head.
O keep us, Love divine, near Thee,
That we our nothingness may know,
And ever to Thy glory be
Walking in faith while here below.
Thou gav'st us Father, in Thy love,
To Christ to bring us home to Thee,
Suited to Thine own thoughts above,
As sons like Him, with Him to be
In Thine own house. There love divine
Fills the bright courts with cloudless joy;
But 'tis the love that made us Thine
Fills all that house without alloy.
O boundless grace! What fills with joy
Our hearts are giv'n e'en now to share.
Which with its radiance fills that sphere -
E'en Christ, of God the power and light -
Our title is that light to share.
O Mind divine, so must it be
That glory all belongs to God!
O Love divine, that did decree
We should be part, through Jesus' blood.
Thy power is with us now,
Most blest is this our portion
Which now, by Thee, we know,
As first of all the fam'lies
And in this place of favour
Our God and Father, we respond anew
To love in Christ revealed, and praise Thy Name.
He did Thy will; and, for the joy in view,
Endured the cross, despising all the shame.
He midst His brethren strikes the note of praise;
We hear His song, our hearts responsive swell;
And on this day when He His voice doth raise,
In spirit enter where we soon shall dwell.
Chosen in Him, Thy well-beloved Son,
We have our part in joy before Thy face;
Predestined, ere this world had yet begun,
For that blest world, where all bespeaks Thy grace,
Sons loved and loving, who Thy house shall fill,
Our endless portion there in love to be;
Each with some trait of Him who loves so well,
For Thy delight and joy eternally.
That we, the church, to glory brought,
Should with the Son be blest?
O God, the thought was Thine,
Fruit of the wisdom, love divine,
For thoughts so bold, so free,
Greatness or strength could ever find;
Made for Thy Son, bone of His bone,
Upon His throne, in glory bright,
The bride of Christ shall be.
Thy wondrous thought has made our boast,
Light of the waiting pilgrim's heart,
Arise, and with Thy morning beams
Come, blessed Lord! bid every shore
The praises of Thy royal name,
And own Thee as their King.
Bid the whole earth, responsive now
Break forth in rapturous strains of joy
O Lord, Thy fair creation groans,
The air, the earth, the sea,
In unison with all our hearts,
Thine was the cross, with all its fruits
Be Thine the crown of glory now,
Has reached us through Thy Son;
We now are one with Him above;
As thus before Thee without blame,
In Him who lives we live;
Our spirits rise to bless Thy Name,
The praises led by Thy Beloved
And we, with hearts divinely moved,
Father, Thy love our portion is;
Thou gav'st us to Thy Son,
For Thine own glory and for His,
O God for ever blest, o'er all supreme,
Our praises rise to Thee, our endless theme;
Clothed with the worth of Christ before Thy face,
As brought to Thee by Him, we know our place.
All things in heav'n and earth proceed from Thee;
In Christ Thy glories infinite we see.
O holy God, we are through Him alone
For evermore accepted as Thine own!
From all eternity Thy sovereign love
Had purposed we this cloudless joy should prove;
Now, by the Spirit's power, we have our part
In the complacent rest of Thine own heart.
Thy wondrous plan, secured in counsels wise,
Reveals Thy glorious day before our eyes.
To Thee, the God of light and love, we sing,
And filled with Thee, our hearts their homage bring.
Our glorious God, how wondrous to be near,
Thy mighty love in Him has brought us here,
O love divine! How wondrous is Thy will
That myriad sons Thy presence blest should fill!
Then, blessed God, Thou all in all shalt be,
New heav'ns and earth, from thraldom ever free,
Christ and the church Thy glory will display
Where Thou dost dwell through that eternal day.
O Holy Spirit of our God,
May Thy blest voice be heard,
Thy voice, so true and constant, speaks
Thy grace we know that freely serves
Thy joy is e'er afresh to show
Thy presence here with saints on earth
Grant us to hear Thy voice.
O God, our hearts are filled with joy,
And praises rich our lips employ,
When Thou wilt manifest Thy power -
When heav'n and earth shall pass away,
Ended for ever death's dark sway;
And Thou wilt then make all things new,
New heav'n and earth bring into view -
When Thou shalt wipe away all tears,
Banish all sorrow, pain and fears:
With rapture then each heart will swell,
When Thou Thyself with men shalt dwell.
The centre blest, and all will see
And Thou, O God, be all in all!
Lord Jesus, Thou by whom the worlds were made,
As holy Babe wast in a manger laid;
Yet did angelic hosts Thy title own,
And highest glory give to God alone.
Thy lowly pathway grace and truth displayed,
But wicked hands Thy brow with thorns arrayed;
Now glory-crowned, blest answer to Thy shame,
Thy saints with joy Thy worthiness acclaim.
To win Thy bride what depths or woe were Thine,
Scorned and betrayed, beset by powers malign!
Thy pierced hands, Thy riven side revealed
The strength of love that by Thy death was sealed.
Most blessed Lord, fain would we learn of Thee
To fill our part, yea, more like Thee to be;
With purpose fixed, Thy path our happy choice,
Thyself our all, until we hear Thy voice.
Holy, holy holy! Blessed God, we praise Thee;
From eternity Thou art, to Thee all glory be!
O what strains adoring, from Thy saints outpouring!
Worship and praise we render unto Thee.
Holy, holy, holy! of Thine own we give Thee;
Thou art evermore the Same, in power and majesty;
Greatness all transcending, glory never ending,
All, all is Thine, Thine only could it be.
Holy, holy, holy! worshipping before Thee,
Lifting holy hands on high, our place Thy sanctuary;
Love in its own dwelling, every voice is telling
Of glory known, yet wondrous mystery.
Holy, holy, holy! hearts and voices blending;
To eternity Thou art! a rev'rent note we raise.
Hear the song unending from Thy sons ascending!
Our glorious God, to Thee be all the praise!
We'd stand a witness here on earth,
A place keep clean for Thee,
In righteousness, faith, love and peace
Should mar our part with Thee,
But faithful in our steadfast walk
From taint of sin be free.
Hold all our hearts for Thee,
Till we behold Thee, Lord Thyself,
To us Thou comest, faithful to Thy word;
Thou dost not leave Thine own as orphans here.
"Peace unto you," Thou sayest, blessed Lord;
The glorious morn has ris'n our hearts to cheer.
And now Thou joyest in Thy saints, O Lord;
Thy banner over us is endless love.
We praise Thee, for Thy presence doth afford
A foretaste of unclouded bliss above.
We'll sing of the Shepherd that died,
That died for the sake of the flock;
His love to the utmost was tried,
But firmly endured as a rock.
What love from this Shepherd did flow,
When in care for the sheep He was led
To stand between them and the foe,
And lay down His life in their stead!
Our song then for ever shall be
Of the Shepherd who gave Himself thus;
No subject's more glorious than He,
No theme more affecting to us.
Of Him and His love will we sing,
His praises our tongues shall employ,
In yonder bright regions of joy.
We wait for Thee, O Son of God,
"A little while" - Thou'lt come, O Lord,
Thus hast Thou said; we lift the head
We wait for Thee, content to share
So meekly Thou the cross didst bear,
How should we not receive with Thee
The cup of shame and sorrow,
We wait for Thee, for Thou, e'en here,
In spirit still we find Thee near,
In cloudless light and glory bright,
We in the air shall meet Thee,
And thus with joy shall greet Thee.
We wait for Thee - Thou wilt arise,
Whilst hope her watch is keeping;
Shall be our years of weeping.
Our hearts beat high, the dawn is nigh
Be to Him who bore the cross,
Who redeemed our souls by tasting
Death, the death deserved by us.
While we tell the wondrous story
Of the Saviour's cross and shame,
Be to God and to the Lamb.
Give ye glory to His Name!
To Thee, blest Holy Spirit, now
How perfect is Thy work divine,
The way of love how blest,
In bringing Christ before our hearts
That love might be at rest!
Thy wondrous glory wakes our song,
Blest Spirit, unto Thee our hearts
Awake, each saint, in joyful lays,
To sing the great Redeemer's praise;
He justly claims a song from thee:
His loving kindness, O how free!
He saw us ruined in the fall,
He saved us from our lost estate:
His loving kindness, O how great!
Though numerous hosts of mighty foes,
Though earth and hell our way oppose,
He safely leads His saints along:
His loving kindness, O how strong!
When trouble, like a gloomy cloud,
Has gathered thick and thundered loud.
He by His church has always stood:
His loving kindness, O how good!
Soon He will call us hence away
To the bright realms of endless day;
There shall we with Himself above
O Holy Spirit, Thee we bless,
Thy Person and Thy power confess;
To Thee our souls in worship bow.
Thou Holy One from heav'n come forth
How great, how glorious, is Thy worth!
With saints on earth now pleased to dwell,
To Thee responsive songs we raise
To Thee devote our joyful praise.
We worship in Thy presence thus,
Rejoicing that Thou art with us.
Of nearness we shall ever know!
To crown the service of this hour.
And Thou dost with unerring skill
Expose its depths, subdue its will.
And let Thy voice be clearly heard
As Thou dost clothe the spoken word.
When Thy great work, in secret might,
Has brought the treasure all to light.
Jesus our Lord, we would joyfully render
Worship and honour and praise to Thy Name!
Peerless, unique in Thy glory and splendour,
Thee we would hail and Thy greatness proclaim.
God over all Thou for ever remainest -
All by the word of Thy pow'r Thou sustainest,
Prostrate in worship before Thee we bow.
Yet in devotion and grace beyond measure,
Lord, Thou didst die to accomplish God's will -
Here as a Man for His glory and pleasure
All the designs of His love to fulfil.
Vanquished all foes, Thou art risen victorious,
Thus to Thine own, Lord, Thou comest all glorious:
Worship and homage we give to Thee now!
Jesus as our Lord to know,
Here to yield Him full allegiance,
With a perfect love He loves us,
Nought its ceaseless flow can stay;
For His pleasure He has bought us,
He Himself is ours for aye.
Never shall His love, so faithful,
If He claims our hearts' affections
That in Him was first made known.
Once on earth in Bethlehem's manger,
As a holy Babe, He lay;
God come down, a heav'nly Stranger,
Sinner, see thy God beside thee,
In a servant's form come near,
Onward still He treads His way,
Jesus died and rose for thee;
God in heav'n now waits to save thee,
Lord Jesus, come, Thy saints for Thee are waiting,
To see Thy face and be with Thee at home;
E'en now our endless bliss anticipating,
With all our hearts we say, "Lord Jesus, come!"
Lord  Jesus, come, our hearts for Thee are longing,
To share Thy joy in those bright courts above,
Where Thou wilt have Thy saints around Thee thronging,
In all the blessed fulness of Thy love.
Lord Jesus, come; with hearts and voices blending,
Soon shall we praise Thee in Thy Father's home;
Soon shall we sing the new song, never ending,
But now we sing to Thee, "Lord Jesus, come!"
Lord Jesus, source of every grace,
Soon shall we see Thee face to face,
Be ever with Thee, hear Thy voice,
The love which doth our hearts rejoice,
Which in that world, for evermore,
We follow Thee, through grace supplied
We hear of war no more,
And, O sweet thought! for ever rest
Blest God and father, we confess
We every grace derive from Thee,
The things that to our peace belong;
Here nothing ill can now intrude,
Nor jarring notes disturb our song.
How may we rise to Thy vast thoughts,
The grace that sets our souls on high,
And love that brings us nearer still?
To wake our richest songs of praise,
And claim our hearts without reserve.
With one resounding note of joy
From many sons who worship Thee -
Conferred on those of high estate,
Are held in love so full, so great.
Lord, in past and distant ages,
Long before the ken of man,
Or the heav'ns and earth began,
Thou wast there in all Thy glory -
Blessed Lord, we bow the knee -
What that love no thought can fathom;
But, in time, Thou wouldst in manhood
Here the Name of God declare,
Which Thou couldst with others share.
All His will Thou hast accomplished,
All the work He gave Thee, done;
One in thought, in plan and purpose,
He the Father, Thou the Son.
To Thine own Thou didst declare
That Thy Father was their Father,
And His love they now might share.
Glory be to God the Father,
As we view the vast creation,
So our minds would move to worship,
But, our God, how great Thy yearning
In Thy house e'en now to praise Thee,
So in Christ, through His redemption
Thou hast brought, in new creation,
Glory be to God the Father,
Our God and father, we draw near to Thee
In all the worth of Thy beloved Son;
All Thou hast e'er desired from man we see
In Him, Thy Christ, Thine own anointed One.
No thought of His e'er moved apart from Thine;
Each holy footstep gave Thee fresh delight;
Perfect expression of Thy will divine
Thou hadst in Him - come forth from glory bright.
Thou ever lovedst Him - ere time began
He was beside Thee - one in all Thou art;
In Godhead counsel one, in that vast plan
In which Thou wouldst make known to men Thy heart.
And now Thou lov'st Him, for Himself He gave -
Theme of our song when time shall cease to be;
Laid down His life that Thou, O God, shouldst have
Fruit of Thy love in sons who worship Thee.
No soul, in this weak mortal hour,
Can grasp the glory that is Thine!
E'en in its thoughts of boundless grace
It leaves us all far, far behind;
The love that gives with Christ a place
And yet that love is not unknown
To those who have the Saviour seen;
Nor strange to those He calls His own,
Pilgrims in scenes where He has been.
In Him Thy perfect love revealed
Has led our hearts that love to trace,
Where nothing of that love's concealed,
But meets us in our lowly place.
And here we walk as sons, through grace,
A Father's love our present joy;
Sons in the brightness of Thy face
Find rest no sorrows can destroy!
What a work has now been done
By Thine own most glorious service
For the Father and the Son!
And the Father's thoughts in glory
Thou dost know the Father's feelings
And His joy in the assembly
Thou art worthy of our praises
As Thy power its strength imparts,
That the Christ, the Head of all things,
May through faith dwell in our hearts.
Christ is the Saviour of sinners,
Christ is the Saviour for me;
Long I was chained in sin's darkness,
Now by His grace I am free.
This is the Saviour for me.
Now I can say I am pardoned,
This is the Saviour for me.
Just as I was He received me,
This is the Saviour for me.
Loved with a love that's unchanging,
Blessed with all blessings so free,
How shall I tell out His praises!
This is the Saviour for me.
Soon shall the glory be dawning,
Then, when His face I shall see,
Sing, O my soul, in thy gladness,
This is the Saviour for me!
God waits in grace with hands outstretched to bless -
Repentance only, God requires from man,
And faith in Christ, His well-beloved Son.
This priceless favour you may now embrace;
Since Jesus suffered in the sinner's place
Blest sinless One! for us He sin was made,
Redemption's price by precious blood was paid.
Unsparing judgment, in that dark, lone hour,
Laid down His life, destroyed death's fearful power;
The mighty Saviour's ris'n and glorified.
God's secret things, long treasured up in heav'n,
Peace, sonship, joy, the Holy Spirit giv'n,
God's word obey, these wondrous blessings share -
The Spirit's comfort, guidance, love and care.
Jesus, our Lord, Thou Morning Star,
How well we know Thy Name!
Jesus, the One who came from heav'n
Thy love and lowliness still shine
Jesus, the One who trod the earth,
Jesus, what memories thrill our hearts
While now to heav'n our eyes we turn
That we may with Thee be;
Heav'n's morning breaks and glory dawns
When Thy blest face we see.
Praise to Thee, our God, belongeth,
In the light that none could know,
All Thy works Thy power show.
Thou art God, supreme Thy throne;
Ever just are all Thy dealings,
And through all, Thy blessed nature -
Thou dost dwell amid the praises
Lord Jesus, may our days on earth
In all our ways our one desire
May Thy blest presence on us shine,
And fill our hearts with joy divine!
May we be given grace to walk
In storm and calm to cleave to Thee,
On Thy strong arm, from danger free,
We have all things in having Thee.
And we know that Thou wouldst have us
In that love for ever living -
Well we know where Thou art dwelling,
Lord, we do not ask the question,
Our God, we bless Thee, glorious source
Both heav'n and earth belong to Thee,
Exalted, Thou, as Head o'er all;
Thy glorious Name our souls revere,
Complacent Thou in love, we see
All things made subject unto Thee.
When all shall know Thy glorious sway,
And love shall be at rest.
Th'eternal scene then filled by Thee -
Thou all in all shalt ever be.
"Thou art that God" to the ages eternal,
Loved and adored by blest myriads of men!
Feeling the warmth of affections paternal,
Fam'lies predestined shall fill earth and heav'n.
Strengthened with might by the Father's own Spirit,
We now by faith hold the Christ in our heart;
Thus apprehending a sphere vast, yet finite,
Love of the Christ passing knowledge our part.
Thou canst, O God, even fill to Thy fullness
Hearts which are stirred by this wonderful theme;
In the assembly, now blest in Christ Jesus,
Be to Thee endlessly glory supreme!
Father, to Thee we now draw near,
With Christ, the Firstborn, to appear,
While endless praise our lips employ
O love so great, so full, so free,
That leads, blest Father, now to Thee,
Thy Spirit strength'ning in our heart,
With Christ to know our heav'nly part,
O Lord, with our ears and hearts open,
Awaiting Thy shout would we be,
The summons that calls us to heaven,
For ever to be Lord, with Thee.
Thy word and Thy Spirit, blest Lover,
The earnest, are giv'n to Thy bride;
Thou'rt near to faith's vision, O Saviour,
But soon she will be at Thy side.
O come then, lord Jesus, we're watching!
And take now Thy spouse home to Thee!
The bride her loved Bridegroom to see.
Thou art, O Lord Jesus, still waiting
With love deep, eternal, we know;
Our hearts in response, with love's burning,
Await Thee, with lamps all aglow.
The Spirit and bride are united
And now with one voice would say "Come!"
Throughout the long night she has waited
To see Thee, her faithful Bridegroom.
Gross darkness the earth doth now cover,
And night like a pall shrouds the land;
Thy flock is still here, Shepherd Lover,
The sheep Thou hast kept by Thy hand.
Midst darkness faith clearly sees beaming
The light of Thy coming afar;
We watch for the dawn of the morning,
And hail Thee, the bright Morning Star.
The word of Thy patience we're keeping,
To meet Thee, the Hope of our heart!
Once slain, but now alive again,
Since we with Him are dead;
Our life is hid with Christ in God,
And we, by faith, in heav'n behold
O the wonder of the moment!
To secure a scene of glory,
Now, in Christ, their wealth is shown
That for men a place in sonship
Might through Him, the Son, be known.
But the objects of that favour
Were in chains of bondage bound;
And the lost must needs be found.
Love was thus in mercy seeking
And the wonder of the story -
Jesus died to save them all!
Thus that work in all it's glory
While His grace o'er all has triumphed,
Here the Spirit too bears witness
To the truth that all is done.
O the wonder of the moment -
We sing to Thee, Lord Jesus,
The charm of Thine own grace.
To be Thy joy for ever,
Fruit of Thine own blest service,
For whom Thou gav'st Thy life;
As of Thee, like Thee, for Thee,
Thee we praise, our God and Father,
Ere the world was, Thou didst choose us
Thou Thine only Son hast given,
For, in love to bring us near Thee,
Father! we Thy sons now call Thee,
Thee we worship, God and Father,
Soon in Thine own house around Thee
For His praise who glorified Thee
Father, spring and source of blessing,
Grateful praise to Thee we bring;
Gladly of Thy love we sing;
Love that found its full expression
Him, who dwelling in Thy bosom,
Has Thy love made fully known.
Now to us in Christ is shown,
For the sons Thou hadst foreknown.
Brought to rest within the circle
There we drink the living waters,
Taste the joys that never fade.
Drawn to Him in boundless grace -
We adore Thee, God and Father,
Praise and worship we would render
We praise Thee, Lord, blest source of deepest joy,
Responsive to Thy voice of holy love;
Thou living spring of bliss without alloy,
Bright inlet to the light of heav'n above!
We praise Thee, Lord, for in Thy blessed face
God's glory shines for us without a veil;
And now Thou leadest us in righteous grace
To that blest place where praises never fail.
We live of Thee, we've heard Thy quick'ning voice
Speaking of love beyond all human thought -
Thy Father's love, in which we now rejoice,
As those in spirit to Thy Father brought.
Thou hast made known the father, whom we've seen
In Thy blest Person - infinite delight!
Yea, it suffices, though we here but glean
Some foretaste of His love, till all be light.
Keeps watch, with an unwearying eye,
To see what fruits His children bear -
Fruits that may suit their calling high;
Takes ever knowledge of our state:
What dims communion with His love,
Might check our growth, or separate
Our hearts from what's revealed above.
O wondrous love! that ne'er forgets
The objects of its tender care;
May chasten still, while sin besets,
To warn and guard them where they are;
Yet ne'er forgets, but feeds them still
With tokens of His tender love;
Will keep till, freed from every ill,
They find their rest with Him above.
Keep near, our souls, to that blest place
Where all those heav'nly glories shine,
Which suit the brightness of His face.
That meets the grace that gave the Son!
That waits to serve Him as His own,
Till grace, what grace began, shall crown!
This world is a wilderness wide;
We have nothing to seek nor to choose;
We've no thought in the waste to abide;
We have nought to regret nor to lose.
For the Lord has Himself gone before;
He has marked out the path that we tread;
It's as sure as the love we adore;
We have nothing to fear nor to dread.
For the path where our Saviour has gone
Has led up to His Father and God,
To the place where He's now on the throne;
And His strength shall be ours on the road.
And with Him shall our rest be on high,
When in holiness bright we sit down,
In the joy of His love ever nigh,
In the peace that His presence shall crown.
'Tis the treasure we've found in His love
That has made us now pilgrims below;
And 'tis there, when we reach Him above,
As we're known, all His fulness we'll know.
And our Saviour! 'tis Thee from on high
We await till the time Thou shalt come,
To take those Thou hast led by Thine eye
To Thyself in Thy heavenly home.
Until then, 'tis the path Thou hast trod
Our delight and our comfort shall be;
We're content with Thy staff and Thy rod,
Till with Thee all Thy glory we see.
O Lord, our hearts are waiting
Which wakes the saints now sleeping,
And to Thee brings them nigh;
Shall meet Thee in the air,
O hour for which in patience
Till all Thy saints are gathered,
O Lord, with shouts of triumph
When brought to Thee so nigh,
To be Thy joy for ever,
And dwell with Thee on high;
To rest in all that brightness,
To which our hearts shall answer,
And then with Thee, blest Saviour,
God and Father, source of glory,
High above our praise art Thou;
Yet in Christ Thou hast declared
Love that makes our spirits bow.
Thou shouldst have this rich delight,
Hearts to swell Thy praise for ever,
Sons to worship in Thy sight.
Thou didst sanctify and send Him,
All Thy counsels to make good -
Him who knew Thine earnest longing,
He no service thought too lowly,
To secure Thy plan so holy,
Now Thy love has found its answer,
All Thy thoughts secured and sealed;
And the sons Thou hast been seeking
Nor toucheth He our hearts in vain:
We praise, we praise Thee, Lord
Rejoice in Him, ye saints, again,
And faith takes up the happy strain:
Our joy is in Thee, Lord.
For ever be the glory giv'n
O Lamb of God, to Thee!
Thyself, O Lord, on earth, in heav'n,
Our theme of joy shalt be.
Our God, from Thy blest heart and mind has spread
The heav'nly light of wisdom all divine,
That we might know in Christ, our living Head,
That which shall e'er all other light outshine.
And wider still, that to the powers above,
Through the assembly, might be now made known
All-various wisdom of that searchless love,
That yet shall bind the universe in one.
Before Thee, Father, we would bow our knees,
That, strengthened by Thy Spirit, Christ may dwell
Within our hearts; and by the love that sees
That all-divine domain, Thy praise we tell.
O love well-known, surpassing all our thought,
Love of the Christ, the climax of all good!
Into eternal sunshine we are brought,
Filled unto all the fulness of our God.
In that bright home of love divine,
There the full rays of glory shine
In Him who stooped to die.
And we shall share that home above
Which He for us has won,
As now we share His Father's love
We shall be with Him where He is,
We shall behold His glory bright -
Behold the Lamb, whose precious blood
The power to make our peace with God,
The dying thief beheld that Lamb
And proved the value of the Name
His soul, by virtue of the blood,
We, too, the cleansing power have known
By grace have learnt His Name to own,
By whom we're brought to God.
To Him, then, let our songs ascend,
Who stooped in grace so low;
To Christ, the Lamb, the sinner's Friend,
Into Thy presence, Lord, we come,
And sit in stillness at Thy feet
To hear The word, so pure, so sweet,
And find in Thee our spirits' home:
By faith e'en now to see Thy face,
And hear Thy words of light and love -
Thy witness of the things above -
The substance, Thou, of truth and grace.
Thus to retire from all around,
And in Thy holy presence be,
Thy beauty, Lord, alone to see,
Thy blessed voice the only sound.
For to our feeble path down here,
In love Thou dost delight to come;
Responsive love gives Thee a home,
Glorious Son of God, to Thee
We to Thee with rev'rence bow,
Thee we hail with homage now.
As the Victor Thou art known,
Bringing peace which sets us free
We rejoice as now we prove
Lord Jesus, our souls would adore Thee,
We render Thee blessing and praise;
In worship and homage before Thee
Our hearts and our voices we raise.
The love that in death thou hast shown,
To Thee who hast made us Thine own.
Thy path of devotion we treasure:
The will of Thy God and His pleasure
We hail Thee as risen and living -
Supreme to us now, Lord, Thou art;
To Thee we are joyfully giving
The worship and praise of our heart!
When, through Thy love's deep pity,
The waves did o'er Thee roll.
For us Thy blood was shed;
For us Thou, Lord of glory,
O Lord, Thou now art risen,
For sin Thou once hast suffered,
Thou liv'st to die no more.
Sin, death and hell are vanquished
And lo! we share Thy triumphs,
We own with Thee we died;
With Thee, our life, we're risen,
From sin, the world, and Satan,
And here would walk as strangers,
Jesus our Lord, of Thee, the King,
Our tribute now we gladly bring
Thine hand hath ope'd these lips once dumb,
To sing of Thee whilst travelling home
Men sing aloud the praise of man,
Whose little life is as a span,
Of Thee our song, God's blessed Son,
In Thee we make our boast -
Is marred by man's ungrateful hand,
This makes the earth, bright though it seem,
No home can we the place esteem
Lord Jesus, here we wait for Thee,
And as we wait we sing.
E'en now the Morning Star we see
Ours then the nobler song to raise,
And find unceasing joy in praise
To Thee in that bright place.
Lord Jesus, when we think of Thee,
Of all Thy love and grace,
Our spirits long and fain would see
And though the wilderness we tread,
Yet in Thy love such depths we see,
Our souls well forth in praise -
Content ourselves, while, Lord, to Thee
Our Lord, our Life, our rest, our Shield,
Our Rock, our Food, our Light;
Each thought of Thee doth constant yield
Blest Saviour, keep our spirits stayed,
Till we, in robes of white arrayed,
Death had on Thee no claim,
He who had death's dread power
Met Thee in that dark hour:
But Thou hast burst the grave,
Out of Thy death has sprung
The mighty God who dwelt in light
As Man came forth the foe to fight,
In perfect light was sin laid bare,
While perfect love in triumph there
Who but the sinless One could be
And who in heaven or earth but He
Could cleanse me with His blood?
To save the sinner Jesus came,
And now my willing lips proclaim
What He hath done for me.
His finished work is all my trust,
Eternal proof that God is just
In all this way of love.
Delivered from the wrath to come,
I soon shall see His face;
And praise, in God's eternal home,
Ye with care and toil opprest,
Come, and I will give you rest.
On the cross He once has suffered,
There by Him the work was done;
And the word by God now uttered
To each weary soul is - Come!
Come! - the Father's house stands open,
With its love and light and song;
All to you may now belong.
From sin's distant land of famine,
To a Father's house of plenty,
Come! - for night is gath'ring quickly
O'er this world's fast fleeting day;
If you linger in the darkness,
You will surely miss your way.
From the world and its delusion -
Now our voices rise as one,
Led Thee to give Thy Son,
To give Thy Well-beloved for us.
What led Thy Son, O God,
To come from heav'n on high,
Led Him to die and suffer thus.
Moved Thee to give Thy Spirit thus.
What love to Thee we owe,
Our God, for all Thy grace!
Gladly, O God, we praise Thee thus
For all Thy boundless love to us.
Praise the Lamb! yes, Thou art worthy,
To redeem Thy saints and make us
Yes, we praise Thee, for Thou lov'st us;
For the peace and joy and gladness
Thine we are, and Thine for ever,
Join with saints from every nation,
Praise the Lamb, for He is worthy,
Thy Son hath brought Thy love to light;
In songs of joy we now unite.
Through Him Thy love is known,
In Him we are brought nigh.
With rev'rence and with love we bow
To Thee, O God, our Father Thou!
We seek Thy gracious help this hour;
Give us to hear Thy voice benign,
Cause us afresh to prove Thy power.
Searcher of depths, the depths of God,
To us, our Guide, fresh grace afford,
As love's domain our hearts explore.
With every thought by Thee controlled,
The truth's pure light would we pursue,
As Thou, blest Spirit, dost unfold
Lord Jesus, Thou hast drawn our hearts,
That we might near Thee be;
Thy bride, the object of Thy love -
We thus are one with Thee.
O wondrous joy in union found,
Thou all in all to us!
Thy holy love fills every heart -
Thy joy to have it thus.
To be for Thee, O Lord, what bliss
The movements of such love as this
That we His face, long loved,
The heart in which Thou dwell'st,
Still, Lord, to see Thy face,
Nor what is next Thy heart
Thy saints, O Lord, with Thee
Son of God, with joy we view Thee
Of God's love the object meet;
While, Lord Jesus Christ, 'tis through Thee
As Thy brethren now we hail Thee,
He who has with glory crowned Thee
Called us to this blessed place.
From the triumph and the glory
Of Thy rest in love divine,
Comes to us the wondrous story,
How God's purpose made us Thine;
How by dying Thou hast freed us
From the man of sin and shame,
That, unhindered, Thou mightst lead us
Now to know Thy Father's name.
We would now abide in love;
Know Thy joy, as those belonging
At Thy feet our hearts would bow,
Who hast brought, in new creation,
Sons of God before Him now.
And a song is sweetly thrilling
Music which God's ear is filling,
Notes which could be only Thine.
God our Father, Thee we worship,
Own the glory of Thy grace;
That with Christ should be our place.
Abba, Father! He who knows Thee
Has Thy Name to us declared;
And Thy love for Him unchanging,
By Thy many sons is shared.
Now Thy glory is before us, -
We, the firstborn ones, adore Thee,
Bless Thee, as in Christ made known!
All Thine own this promise share;
Patience waits, while love is yearning
For Thy presence in the air.
And the living changed shall be
When, caught up through glory's portal,
As Thou art in heav'nly glory,
Thine own image we shall bear -
And Thy throne and kingdom share.
Filled with joy beyond all measure
When Thy glorious face we see!
Jesus, our Lord, we assemble together,
Here to remember Thyself whom we love,
For as Thine own we are feeling Thine absence,
Though we delight in Thy glory above.
Now, Lord, together in blessed communion,
Praise we Thy Name as Thyself we await.
Soon shalt Thou take Thine appointed dominion,
Soon shalt appear in Thy royal estate.
Till Thine outshining Thy death we are showing,
Owning Thee thus as the One without peer;
Whilst, lord, that death of such shame and deep suff'ring
Unto Thy lovers Thyself doth endear.
For Thou hast loved us with love never failing,
Laid down Thy life for us, given Thine all.
Love strong as death has been proved and has triumphed,
Love which our hearts shall for ever enthrall.
When Christ will claim His own;
We soon shall hear that voice of power;
Lord Jesus, Thy return draws nigh,
We long to see Thy face.
Radiant and pure, in light divine,
What tides of praise shall flow!
For Thee to take us home;
Fulfil to us Thy gracious word.
From scenes of conflict, burden, grief and care,
To Thy blest presence, Lord, we now repair;
Thy shadow here provides a calm retreat,
Where sympathies divine our frailty meet.
To Thee the cause of every sigh is known,
Thou who dost feel the sorrows of Thine own;
Unspoken fears, and questions hard to solve,
Before the rays of heav'nly light dissolve.
Thy well-proved love our confidence inspires
To count upon the grace that never tires;
So would we make Thine interests, Lord, our care,
And with thanksgiving wait on Thee in prayer.
Shed for rebels, shed for sinners,
Telling that the work is finished;
Thought Thy sins are red like crimson,
Jesus' precious blood can make them
Precious blood, our song and glory,
O blessed God, we praise Thee,
That we, in Christ, before Thee,
Should share the Son's blest place;
O what a Saviour is Jesus the Lord!
Well may His Name by His saints be adored!
He has redeemed them from hell by His blood,
Saved them for ever, and brought them to God.
Now in the glory He waits to impart
Peace to the conscience, and joy to the heart;
Waits to be gracious, to pardon and heal
All who their sin and their wretchedness feel.
Thousands have fled to His spear-pierced side;
Welcome they all have been, none are denied;
Weary and laden, they all have been blest;
Joyfully now in the Saviour they rest.
Blessed God, with Christ before Thee
We approach, in love set free;
This - the product of Thy counsels,
Formed to praise throughout the ages -
In Thy presence is at rest.
Vessel filled e'en to Thy fulness,
In Thine own domain of glory
Fills Thy heart with deep delight.
Blest Son of God, we worship Thee;
To hearts that wait for Thee alone
Thou camest in of old and all
And now amidst Thine own Thy praise
Thou hast a glory far beyond
Yet pleased to come, as lowly Man,
Thou hast come in on God's behalf
Firstborn of all to lead the throng
We praise and worship as we see
And love that, giving all, secures
O teach us more of Thy blest ways,
And fix and root us in Thy grace,
O tell us often of Thy love,
Of all Thy grief and pain;
And let our hearts with joy confess
That thence comes all our gain.
For this, O may we freely count
Vain things of earth but dross;
The dearest object of our love,
Engrave this deeply on our hearts
That we may, in a fuller way,
Thou dwellest now, O God, midst fragrant praise
Resulting from Thine own great work and ways;
Th'assembly in Christ Jesus - ever blest,
And filled to all Thy fulness - is at rest.
In the Beloved favour now is known
By her whom Christ can call with joy His own;
For whom in love He gave Himself - His bride -
To be with Him in glory, by His side:
Abiding peace, joy ne'er to fade away;
Off'rings for God are in abundance brought,
Willing response for all that Thou hast wrought.
To bear Thy yoke, and learn from Thee,
The mind and heart to fill;
Thy patient life - to calm the soul;
Sing aloud the story of His victory!
How He left the splendour of His home on high,
Came in love so tender, on the cross to die.
Yes! He came from heaven, suffered in our stead;
Praise to Him be given, Firstborn from the dead!
Jesus, meek and lowly, came the lost to save;
He, the Victim holy, triumphed o'er the grave.
Christ is Lord of glory, sing we now today.
Tell abroad the story; own His rightful sway!
Sing aloud, and never cease to spread His fame;
Triumph, now and ever, in the Saviour's name.
Till Thou comest, Thou art serving
All Thine own in time of need.
Love that bears us all the way
On Thine arm, until we enter
Till the pilgrim path is done;
Thou wilt guide us safely home.
What thought storms may rage against us?
Nought can part us from Thy love!
Well we know Thy hands uplifted -
Thou art on the throne above.
O wilt thou to the Saviour come?
This hour He waits for thee,
To cleanse Thy conscience, fill Thy heart,
Let not Thy sins keep thee away,
Since on the cross He died;
And from the dead was raised that we
O see Him there at God's right hand,
That thou His grace canst prove.
Whate'er thy need He'll meet it now,
Take from His hand the blessing free,
The Holy Spirit, too, He'll give,
To fill Thy heart with joy,
To fill thy life with power divine,
And when to glory thou art come,
The joys that thou hast found
Will make, while endless ages roll,
Thou lead'st our hearts to that blest place
There will Thy love find perfect rest,
Where all in Thee supremely blest,
Where love has found its rest;
And, filled with Thee, the constant mind
There Christ, the centre of the throng,
But not an eye those hosts among
Thy counsels too in all Thine own,
Spread wide the glory of Thy throne,
Yet deeper, if a calmer, joy
And every heart find sweet employ
Nor is its sweetness now unknown,
Well proved in what it's done;
Our Father's love with joy we own,
O praise the Saviour for His love,
To take one to Himself above!
These blessed words our hearts suffice -
He knows His sheep, they hear His voice,
Are owned by Him, His sovereign choice.
Then praise Him, God's beloved Son,
Who has o'er death the vict'ry won!
How better far than earth's rewards!
In life or death we are the Lord's!
In Christ shall all be made alive.
For one He loved and called His own!
The love of God exceeds our boast,
In Father, Son and Holy Ghost.
Yes! God will bring them: every ear
The Lord's assembling shout shall hear.
They'll rise, and we with them shall be
Caught up to dwell, O Lord, with Thee.
We'll be for ever with Thee, Lord!
O Lord, how blest - as day by day
We pass along our pilgrim way -
To know that we are Thine!
Which cleansed, which brought us nigh to God
Thine, ever Thine - to be with Thee,
For where Thou art Thine own must be;
With Thee by those Thou hast declared
Through grace to be Thine own.
O Lord, in meek and godly fear
To follow and to serve Thee here
To be for Thee where Thou hast been,
Until we reach Thee in that scene
Where Thou wilt own us Thine.
Lord, may we always own Thy claim,
And by the daily manna fed,
Renewed in strength, the path we'd tread
Which leads us up to Thee.
Glory, Lord, is Thine for ever,
Ever blest - Thou art the Son!
Great the glory Thou art given,
And the glory Thou hast won;
Great the glory and the splendour
Lord of glory, Thou didst enter
This dark world of sin and woe;
Great Thy glory that was witnessed
By Thine own while here below.
Thou didst die, and now we praise Thee
For in death Thou hast declared
All the fulness of God's love.
Yes, we see Thee crowned with glory,
Is the light that shines in heav'n.
Than the glory Thou hast won;
Thee - the great "I AM" - we worship,
We bless Thee, Holy Spirit, Thou
To whom our hearts adoring bow;
As those whose sins are all forgiv'n,
Whose glorious Lord is Christ in heav'n,
We marvel at Thy lowly grace,
That Thou shouldst come to take Thy place
To undertake in all our need,
We thank Thee for Thy faithful love,
Blest Spirit, hast Thy gracious work,
That not a spot may hidden lurk;
Let not our light be burning dim;
Cause all the saints to cry to Him,
His voice we'll hear, His face we'll see,
As, rising, changed, and still with Thee,
All that our God would give
To plead that all this joy
Else what is now so near
Come, yield to Christ as Lord,
Now in simple faith, Lord Jesus,
Meets the need for every hour;
All my fears dispels for ever
Lord, be Thou my comfort ever;
Saviour, I would claim Thee mine;
For Thy richest love and blessing
Spring of peace art Thou to me;
Keep me still Thy grace enjoying
Who can tell the wondrous measure
Of the love upon me poured?
Thou comest, O Lord, to Thine own;
O'er death and the grave now victorious,
With joy we acclaim Thy renown.
Thy saints in the blaze of Thy glory,
But in manhood's form Thou camest,
Theme of praise that ne'er shall end.
Here the Son, Thy Father loving,
Thou didst in His will delight;
O how pleasing in His sight!
Thoughts divine Thou hast made known,
That there should be men made like Thee -
Those whom Thou canst call Thine own.
Known in bonds so full and deep,
Drawn together, Lord, so near Thee
Thou our hearts in love dost keep.
Praise to Thee we gladly bring;
Of Thy glory now we sing.
I've found a Friend, O such a Friend!
He loved me ere I knew Him;
He drew me with the cords of love,
And thus He bound me to Him.
And round my heart still closely twine
Those ties which nought can sever;
For I am His and He is mine
I've found a Friend, O such a Friend!
He shed His blood to save me;
And not alone the gift of life,
But His own self He gave me.
Nought that I have mine own I call,
I hold it for the Giver;
My heart, my strength, my life, my all
Are His, and His for ever.
I've found a Friend, O such a Friend,
So kind, and true, and tender!
So wise a Counsellor and Guide,
From Him who loves me now so well,
What power my soul shall sever?
Shall life or death, shall earth or hell?
No! I am His for ever.
We see Thee, Lord of glory,
Of God come down in love.
Of all that life of woe,
In which Thy grace was winning
Poor man his God to know!
That Thou shouldst with us be,
We love Thee for Thy meekness
Of love that's come to heal.
To move Thy heart to haste.
The strong man in his armour
Love, that made Thee a mourner
In this sad world of woe,
Of grace that brought Thee low.
O Lord, Thy love's sweet savour
We trace Thy path of love.
No eye was found to pity,
No heart to bear Thy woe,
But shame, and scorn, and spitting:
None cared Thy Name to know.
When Thou didst taste the horror
To death Thy feet did bear.
Love still its power was wielding
Love that made Thee a mourner,
It is not man's to tell!
We worship when we see Thee
We long soon to be with Thee
Who bore for us the wrath!
And take us to Thee - home.
Father, praise to Thee we give;
In Thy favour now we live;
And the light from heav'n above.
Praise to Thee, O Lord, we bring,
Christ the Prophet, Priest and King;
Glad we raise our sweetest strain
To the Lamb that once was slain.
Praise to Thee, the Holy Ghost,
'Tis through Thee that now we live,
Blest our portion. thus to be
Thou our voices lov'st to hear,
We love, Lord Jesus, to recall
Thyself, for Thou hast giv'n Thine all
To Thee in thankfulness we turn,
With souls that glow, with hearts that yearn
By love constrained, Thy death we deem
Our point of severance from this scene
Where man Thy rights did spurn;
To us earth stands in shadow now,
No earth bound prospect would we know,
But stand expectant while we show
Thy death as years roll on.
Thy perfect love our strength shall be
To hold in faith and constancy
The ground that Thou hast won.
Lord Jesus, we rejoice that Thou
Thy love all distance must remove,
And draw us near to Thee;
And by the Spirit now we prove
The love that sets us free.
Its rights belong to Thee alone,
Thou dost our hearts as one unite
Thy beauties fill our raptured sight,
The night is far spent, and the day is at hand;
No sign to be looked for; the Star's in the sky.
Rejoice then, ye saints, 'tis your Lord's own command;
Rejoice, for the coming of Jesus draws nigh.
How bright then that day when the Saviour appears!
How welcome to those who have shared in His cross!
A crown incorruptible then will be theirs,
A rich compensation for suff'ring and loss.
No loss in this world can compare with that day,
With glory that then from heav'n be revealed.
The Saviour is coming, His people may say,
Our Lord whom we look for, our Sun and our Shield.
Lord, kindle within us a holy desire,
Like that which was found in Thy people of old.
Who tasted Thy love, and whose hearts were on fire,
While waiting, in patience, Thy face to behold.
Worthy of homage and of praise,
Worthy by all to be adored,
Thou, Thou art worthy, Jesus, lord!
To Thee e'en now our song we raise,
Thought sure the tribute mean must prove;
No mortal tongue can tell Thy ways,
So full of life, and light, and love.
Yet, Saviour, Thou shalt have full praise;
We soon shall meet Thee on the cloud;
We soon shall see Thee face to face,
In glory praising as we would.
Come, rich and poor; come, old and young,
Through Him who now in glory sits
At God's right hand in heav'n.
O feast upon the love of God,
For Christ His Son has died!
And God commends His wondrous love
O sinner, come, the Saviour waits
O Lord, Thou art, and wast, and art to come,
The great I AM, to Thee be honour, praise!
The First and Last, the Living One who died,
Behold Thou livest now to endless days.
Now Thou appearest to th'assemblies here,
Their works of faith and love Thou dost recall.
We hear Thy voice afresh so loud and clear,
O Jesus Lord, and at Thy feet we fall.
Holy and True amidst departure sore,
Thy faithful word reviewing all our ways,
Thy feet like brass, Thy voice like waters deep,
Our hearts laid bare before Thy searching gaze.
Thy precious words to him that overcomes
Stir fresh desires to serve and honour Thee,
To keep Thy word, and not deny Thy Name,
Till Thou shalt come and we shall with Thee be.
Lord Jesus, as gathered before Thee
Our thoughts and our hearts would combine
To guard Thy great interests so holy,
The glory and fame that are Thine:
Thy guidance and help we are needing,
Our words by the Spirit controlled,
And thus we would now be proceeding -
O come, let Thy mind here unfold!
The darkness around we are feeling,
The love of the many grown cold,
O Lord, let Thy light, pure, revealing,
Shine forth as the truth now is told.
May we be found faithful, abiding
In Thee, suff'rings here to endure!
O Lord, grant the power of discernment,
Thus faithfully would we be caring,
Whilst Thou from this world art away,
Until on Thy throne we are sharing
In headship in Thy coming day.
Lord Jesus Christ, our living Head,
To Thee as God we bow.
Yet we, to Thee, in majesty,
But in Thy manhood's glorious state
For of Thy body, Lord, are we,
Great source of wisdom, power and food,
Thou on Thy church, Thy fulness here,
So unto Thee, our glorious Head,
In nearness, by the Spirit's power,
Our woe is Thine, Lord Jesus;
Our joy is in Thy love;
But woe and joy all lead us
To Thee we look, Lord Jesus,
To Thee whose love we know;
We wait the power that frees us
We greet the day that's nearing,
When all this woe shall cease.
But O for us, blest Saviour,
To be with Thee for ever,
To see Thee who hast loved us,
Whose grace at first had moved us
To taste and know Thy love!
With Thee, O Lord, for ever
Nor act, nor thought shall ever
Shine forth on us through Thee.
O come then soon, Lord Jesus,
Await the power that frees us -
And in the circle of Thy love
In Thee He ever finds delight,
To Thy blest Name, O Lord, we cling,
To Thy sure word we bow.
Teach us that Name to own,
Hark! hark! the voice of Christ, the sinner's Saviour,
In glory seated on His father's throne,
Telling of love and everlasting favour
For sinners far from God, by sin undone.
Message of Jesus, message of love,
Telling of welcome to that bright home above!
Blest words! they speak to us of God's salvation,
Worked out by Christ alone upon the cross,
Who by His blood redeems from every nation,
And saves His people from eternal loss.
Message of Jesus, message of love,
Telling of welcome to that bright home above!
Soon Jesus' voice of love may cease appealing,
And, to your loss, the door of mercy close;
Spurn not the voice of Him with heart so feeling,
Who proved His love by dying for His foes.
Message of Jesus, message of love,
Telling of welcome to that bright home above!
O Lord, as now we gather to Thy Name
Here in the scene of Thy reproach and shame,
Our minds are filled with precious thoughts of Thee,
And of Thy word, This do, remember me.
We view these emblems and would Thee recall,
The One who in Thy love hast giv'n Thine all;
Such wondrous giving that we fain would be
Yielded in mind and heart, O Lord, to Thee.
So now, as one, our willing voices raise
A song of love, rejoicing in Thy praise;
Our hearts exult in thankfulness to Thee,
For Thine almighty love has set us free.
In Thy presence now we worship,
Moves our souls with one accord.
Glorious Son of God, we hail Thee,
Love and might and endless glory
Thou art Lord in Thine own Person,
