Unto Thee our song we're singing,
As we praise Thee, love is bringing
Its own portion for Thy heart.
Who, us to save from loss,
Didst taste the bitter cup of death
'Tis in Thy faithful love we trust
Our Guide and Strength wilt be,
Where the saints in glory thronging,
Where they feed on life's blest Tree -
There is stilled each earnest longing,
Rest - where toil shall be no more;
Peace - where strife shall all be o'er:
Free, our peaceful feet may venture
Christ, the fruit of life and Giver -
Worship, joy and praise are Thine.
Blest God and Father, we respond to Thee,
Thy sons, brought near with Christ, before Thy face
In perfect love and holy liberty;
No cloud to dim the glory of this place.
Our Father Thou, whom Jesus has revealed,
His Father whom He loves, His glory Thine;
He, Thine eternal joy, Himself did yield
To bring to pass Thy thoughts of love divine.
Thy heart, our God, made known - all, all is told!
The purpose of Thy love all time before,
The Spirit to our hearts doth now unfold,
And moves our souls to worship and adore.
O circle of affections all divine,
The foretaste of eternity's bright scene,
Where all the glories of Thy love shall shine
In everlasting joy, and peace serene!
Jesus ready waits to save you,
Full of pity, love and power:
He is willing, doubt no more.
Let not conscience make you linger,
Is to feel your need of Him:
Lost and ruined by the fall;
If you tarry till you're better,
You will never come at all:
O Lord, it is Thyself; none, none but Thee,
Could so call forth response from every heart;
The love that stood the test of Calv'ry's tree
Doth to our longing souls fresh joy impart.
That precious love, Lord Jesus, so well known,
Awakens songs of joy and praise to Thee.
We love Thee, Lord, Thy holy claim we own;
And, by the Spirit moved, we worship Thee.
Our times are in Thy hand;
Our life, our souls, our all, we leave
Our times are in Thy hand;
Pleasing or painful, dark or bright,
As best may seem to Thee.
Our times are in Thy hand;
Why should we doubt or fear?
Our Father's hand will never cause
Our times are in Thy hand;
Now leads His own with tender care,
Our times are in Thy hand;
No creature power from love divine
Our times are in Thy hand;
Till we have left this weary land,
God and Father, we Thy children
Would in meekness hear Thy word;
As Thy Spirit strikes the chord;
All Thy mind we would be learning,
As the desert path we trace;
Thine we are, and would be leaning
Heights of glory Thou hast giv'n,
And our eyes by faith are seeing
Christ at Thy right hand in heav'n;
As on earth His path was trodden,
As the Man of all Thy counsels,
When with joy we thus behold Him,
When His greatness fills our sight,
Then our hearts bow down before Him,
God our Father, Thee we worship,
All Thy boundless love e'en now.
May we therefore still be learning,
In Thy word Thy counsels trace,
Till the day that Thou displayest
All the glory of Thy grace!
O the love of God is boundless,
Doubts have vanished, fears are groundless,
Now I know that love to me.
Love, the source of all my blessing,
Love that set itself on me;
Love that gave the spotless Victim,
O the cross of Christ is wondrous!
There I learn God's heart to me;
Light and love alike are telling
What yon woe and suff'rings mean.
My guilt was borne by Jesus
When in darkness on the tree.
O the sight in heav'n is glorious!
Him, who met the claims of glory
And the need of ruined man
On the cross - O wondrous story! -
God has set at His right hand.
In hope we lift our wishful, longing eyes,
Waiting to see the glorious Sun arise;
How bright, how gladsome will His advent be
When He shines forth in radiant majesty!
How will our eyes to see His face delight,
Whose love has cheered us through the darksome night!
How will our ears drink in His well-known voice,
Whose faintest whisper makes our souls rejoice!
No stain within, no foes or snares around;
No jarring notes shall there discordant sound;
All pure without, all pure within the breast;
No thorns to wound, no toil to mar our rest.
If here on earth the thoughts of Jesus' love
Lift our poor hearts this weary world above:
If even here the taste of heav'nly springs
So cheers the spirit that the pilgrim sings:-
What will the sunshine of His glory prove!
What the unmingled fulness of His love!
What hallelujahs will His presence raise!
What but one loud eternal burst of praise!
For Thou hast e'er a glory
And this Thy due with gladness
Hope of our hearts, O Lord, art Thou,
Thou wilt shine forth, and chase the night
No resting place we seek on earth,
Our eye is on the crown above,
What is it to the brighter hope
There near Thy heart upon the throne,
What grace was in the suff'ring Lamb,
Who died to make us free.
Lord, we rejoice that Thou art gone
To sit upon Thy Father's throne;
Thy path of shame and suff'ring o'er,
Thy heart shall grieve and mourn no more.
With joy our wond'ring hearts retrace
Thy ways on earth of power and grace;
We sit as learners at Thy feet,
Thy words than honey far more sweet.
We gaze with wonder at Thy cross,
With all its suff'ring, shame and loss,
Where Thou for us wast crucified,
And, for our sins, a victim died.
We love to look within the tomb,
Robbed by Thy death of all its gloom;
The stone for ever rolled away:
Thy death the power of death did slay.
We joy to see Thee, Lord, arise
And hear all heav'n united own
Thee worthy to ascend the throne.
Lord, now we wait for Thee to come,
And take us to Thy Father's home;
Why unbelieving? Why wilt thou spurn
Love that so gently pleads thy return?
Why not, believing, come to the Lord?
Trust in the Saviour, doubt not His word.
Why unbelieving? Thou canst be blest,
Jesus will pardon, He'll give thee rest.
Come, ere it be too late,
O Holy Spirit, Thee we worship now,
As God Himself, to cause our hearts to bow,
And move afresh by Thee in heart and soul,
We own Thy power and Thee as God extol.
God is sending out the message
Of His wondrous love and grace,
Sends it from the highest glory,
O this precious light is telling
God's full favour now to man;
From the glory it is streaming -
Ne'er such news since time began!
God has full delight in Jesus,
He has died, and through His dying
All God's pleasure will be done.
In the One who came to die,
Of God's Son enthroned on high!
God has given all to Jesus,
All shall prosper in His hand;
Every knee shall bow to Jesus,
Come, then, trust this peerless Saviour,
Prove the riches of His grace;
Live for ever in God's favour
As it shines in Jesus face!
I could not do without Thee,
Why will you do without Him?
The word of God is true:
The world to doom is passing,
Shall dawn on you or me;
Why will you risk the peril
But with Him - O with Jesus!
To fill with Christ in grace,
As bride and wife, her place!
For Him whose bride Thou art,
Doth dwell so near to men;
And moved by Christ to praise!
O God supreme, we bless Thee,
For of Thee, through Thee, for Thee
Now our praise we sing to Thee.
Heaven's joys, which Thou hast taught us,
We would bow our hearts in homage,
O we wonder at Thy patience!
Spirit, Thou, of truth, who leadest
Thus would our hearts in quietness
And find in these sweet moments
Though all the beasts on earth be slain
To wash away sin's crimson stain,
Though all their blood should flow,
The sacrifice would be in vain,
It needs, the conscience to appease,
No blood hath virtue to atone
For man's offence, but His alone
His, who could say, Himself the Son,
That with the Father He is one,
Jesus the Christ, on earth His Name,
He came - in love to sinners came -
And bowed His head and died;
A full atonement now is made,
The ransom by Himself is paid,
That sinners might draw near to Him,
God planned this great, this gracious scheme,
Let all His saints their voices raise,
And sing the great Redeemer's praise
Fills all that home of love.
And countless tongues in heav'n unite
To tell what He hath done.
With saints in light to dwell;
And now we chant His praises sweet,
Whose love we know so well.
E'en now we taste the love,
By which we'll rise to realms above
For He who suffered once is there,
While myriad saints Christ's likeness bear,
And have with Him their part.
For us the cross He bore;
Now all is Yea, and all Amen,
O glorious Lord! what thoughts Thy mind did fill,
When from Thy God Thou cam'st to do His will!
How deep, indeed, the joy that filled Thy heart -
That myriad sons with Thee should find their part!
Thy brethren, Lord, Thine own and one with Thee,
Were in Thy heart - that they should with Thee be;
Thy church complete and in Thy beauty dressed;
The day of God, and love divine at rest.
O blessed Lord, what treasured thoughts unfold
In light divine, as we Thy face behold!
Now on our view unbounded glories break,
That speak Thy fame and songs eternal wake.
We trace Thy path of love,
Thou who in love couldst stoop so low;
Till Thou dost come Thy death we show.
Our hearts are moved, blest Lord,
With one accord, as thus set free,
We gladly now respond to Thee.
And He doth all my need supply
Doth make this earth a desert drear,
My soul no loss nor sorrow knows
Though long and hard the road,
Faith's eyes are on the goal;
He uses trials for my good,
Thy staff and rod are my resource,
To this great end Thy steps I trace,
Thy face I soon shall see,
I have in Thee full victory,
Thy Name must live, whatever names may die;
It must fill all the earth, as heav'n on high.
Jesus! Thy Name by all shall yet be known,
All kings and nations shall Thy greatness own.
Thou livest, Saviour, and all grace is there,
That with such beauty shone in Thee down here;
No trait is lost, each beauteous grace we see,
All brought through death to shine eternally.
Our joy is full - we have Thee, Jesus, still;
The glory bright Thy precious Name doth fill;
What holds Thy people now while here on earth
Is what Thou art in all Thy wondrous worth.
O Lord, when we the path retrace
Which Thou on earth hast trod,
To man Thy wondrous love and grace,
Thou didst Thy Father's name confess,
Thy path, uncheered by earthly smiles,
Thy love, by man so sorely tried,
Though man in hatred pierced Thy side,
We wonder at Thy lowly mind,
And fain would like Thee be,
And all our rest and pleasure find
We draw nigh in all our need,
In the Name of Him alone
Who for us in heav'n doth plead.
May Thy holy Name be praised
Now on earth as 'tis in heav'n;
May Thy glory high be raised,
Here on earth beset by foes,
Well beloved by Christ her Head,
May the church in love's repose.
May the Christ dwell in our heart,
Known in love past human ken:
Counsel deep and vast for men.
May we here our strength renew,
Run the race with Him in view,
Faint not here, but walk in love.
Lord Jesus Christ, our voices rise as one
Amongst Thine own we would exalt Thy Name,
To Thee, O King of kings and Lord of lords,
Our song would be. Thy glories strike the chords.
The morning stars together once did raise,
Their glorious lays, as later Israel's praise
Celestial hosts break forth around the throne
Worthy art Thou! We join the great refrain;
O Root of David Thou, the Lamb once slain,
To Him who is, who was and is to come,
Be glory now as we extol Thy fame!
Ours is a pardon bought with blood,
Amazing truth! the blood of One
Lay claim to heav'n's eternal throne!
Could bear the stroke that justice aimed;
For none but He, in heav'n or earth,
Could offer that which justice claimed.
But He, the Lord of glory, came;
Upon the cross He bowed His head;
He suffered pain, He suffered shame,
And lay a prisoner with the dead.
But lo! He's risen from the grave,
And bears the greatest, noblest Name:
The Lord - almighty now to save
From sin, from death, from endless shame.
O Lord, we joy that Thou art glory-crowned,
Who by Thy death to God hast brought us nigh;
In Thee alone is our forgiveness found,
And everlasting praises rise on high.
We praise Thee, for Thou didst in death lay down
Thy precious life, an off'ring once for all;
For ever cleansed by blood, our joy and crown
We owe to Thee, and thus before Thee fall.
We bless Thee, glorious Lord; Thou risen art;
And we, set free from sin and death, rejoice
To know in Thee, in life, our endless part,
As with adoring thoughts our praise we voice.
Soon Thou art coming, Lord; we wait for Thee!
Soon all Thine own shall meet Thee in the air,
And we shall dwell with Thee eternally,
All changed, and like to Thee, Thy place to share.
Who died to set us free;
No earthly songs can joy afford
Love that for us atonement made,
Love that has made us Thine.
Thy words of grace, with mercy rife,
Love, that on death's dark vale
Where sin o'er all seemed to prevail,
And now we see Thee ris'n,
Who once for us hast died,
Soon wilt Thou take Thy throne,
And bring us with Thee as Thine own,
With Thee to have our part;
What can full joy and blessing be
No more to grieve Thy heart
But join Thee where Thou art,
O Lord, what joy will fill
To have Thine own with Thee
To loose the bands of death,
To see Thy bride at last
Thy kin is she, O Lord,
With glad acclaim Thy holy Name,
Where every whit Thy glory tells
As sons we raise our hymn of praise
The voice of Christ is heard o'er all
Thy Name is shared as now declared
As is Thy Name so is Thy praise;
Father, to Thee all glory be
When peace like a river attendeth my way,
Whatever my lot, Thou hast taught me to say,
It is well, it is well with my soul.
Though Satan should buffet, though trials should come,
That Christ hath regarded my helpless estate,
And hath shed His own blood for my soul.
My sins - O the bliss of this glorious thought -
My sins - not in part but the whole -
Were borne on the cross, and are gone evermore.
Praise the Lord, praise the Lord, O my soul!
O Lord, 'tis for Thee, for Thy coming we wait,
The sky, not the grave, is our goal.
O voice of archangel! O trumpet of God!
Blessed hope! blessed rest of my soul!
And on the cross He bled;
To free Thee from the bonds of sin,
And give Thee peace and joy within.
And all the road He trod,
Who now is free, at such a cost,
To offer mercy to the lost.
He waits with us to share
His Father's house - that home so bright -
He on the cross must die,
Yes, Jesus' precious blood must flow,
Our sins' full weight must fall
For nothing less could God accept
In payment of that fearful debt.
He bore sin's penalty so dread,
When on the cross His blood He shed.
To pay the debt we owed.
And love to Him did all fulfil.
Of mercy now so richly shed,
For Jesus liveth who was dead.
'Twas not for our great love to Thee
That Thou didst send Thy Son;
That spring of love, O God, we see
What love, Lord Jesus, brought Thee down
To be despised and spit upon,
The sins of many Thou didst bear,
Of all who look to Thee,
When God, Thy God, forsook Thee there,
Ere Thou didst yield Thy breath!
The veil was rent, and God draws nigh
For far and wide the news is borne
Yes. peace! since every claim is met,
And Thou, our peace, art ris'n, and set
Thy grace, O Lord, alone revealed
We thank Thee, and ourselves we yield
O God, Thou source of endless bliss and joy,
Thy praise and worship our full hearts employ,
As, with the Firstborn, we Thy sons now see
The glory that is Thine eternally.
Thine own blest Spirit giv'n - O wondrous plan
To have near Thee with Christ, who for them died,
Suited to Thine own thoughts, men glorified!
How blest Thy grand conceived economy!
Yet Thou dost dwell, in Thine own majesty,
In realms of light where foot has never trod -
The high and lofty, the eternal God!
How sweet is the story of God's boundless love,
That brought His blest Son from the glory above!
Who died in our stead upon Calvary's tree,
Obtaining redemption that we might be free.
How wondrous the story! the claims of the throne
Were met by the blood which for guilt did atone;
The judgment of sin has been borne by the Son,
Who glorified God in the work He has done.
How brilliant the glory where Christ is enthroned!
How rightly His Name above others is owned!
Yes, Jesus, the Saviour, the glory-crowned Lord,
Is worthy by all to be ever adored.
How great is the gift that the Father now gives
To him who obeys and on Jesus believes!
The Spirit, who filleth the heart with God's love,
Himself the blest Earnest of glory above.
It is not with uncertain step
A well-known voice has called us up
The voice of Him who here has trod
(And marked the road which leads to God)
Where once we, lost, did stray.
He leaves us not alone to trace
But leads us still, with living grace,
See! open stands the heav'nly door,
To light the way He's gone before,
In patience then we tread the road -
And trust the love which bears each load,
Our hearts from grief to hide.
God, from His throne on high,
Gave His own Son to die,
His only Son, in wondrous grace,
And dwell in love before His face.
The mighty One, of all things Lord;
And bring the wand'rer home to God.
And old and young may learn His love.
And one and all His goodness prove.
Through toil, and grief, and loss,
The Man of sorrows wends His way;
And now is crowned in brightest day.
Come as you are in all your sin;
By Christ, the door, now enter in.
So full of grace and glory,
So new and yet so old.
And now again we tell it,
So rich, so full, so free;
He who was rich in glory
That we might know God's favour,
How dark that night of sorrow
And lives the lost to save.
Made like to His own image,
To dwell with Him in light.
And is it so, we shall be like Thy Son?
Is this the grace which He for us has won?
Father of glory! Thought beyond all thought!
In glory to His own blest likeness brought.
And yet it must be so! A perfect state
To meet Christ's perfect love - this we await;
The Spirit's hopes, desires, in us inwrought,
Our present joy - with living blessings fraught.
The heart is satisfied, can ask no more;
All thought of self is now for ever o'er!
Christ, its unmingled Object, fills the heart
In blest adoring love - its endless part.
I heard the voice of Jesus say,
Lay down, thou weary one, lay down
I came to Jesus as I was,
I found in Him a resting place,
And He has made me glad.
I heard the voice of Jesus say,
Stoop down, and drink, and live.
I came to Jesus, and I drank
My thirst was quenched, my soul revived,
And now I live in Him.
I heard the voice of Jesus say,
I am this dark world's Light;
Look unto Me: Thy morn shall rise
And all Thy day be bright.
I looked to Jesus, and I found
In Him my Star, my Sun;
And in that light of life I'll walk
O Jesus, Lord, who loved us like to Thee?
Fruit of Thy work, with Thee, too, there to see
Thy glory, Lord, while endless ages roll,
Thy saints the prize and travail of Thy soul.
Yet it must be, Thy love had not its rest
Were Thy redeemed not with Thee fully blest;
That love that gives not as the world, but shares
All it possesses with its loved co-heirs.
Nor we alone, Thy loved ones all, complete,
In glory round Thee there with joy shall meet;
All like Thee, for Thy glory like Thee, Lord:
Object supreme of all, by all adored.
Thy will, O Lord, be done, whate'er the cost
To us, who but for Thee had still been lost;
For Thou hast set us free Thy will to do,
And Thou art set in love to bring us through.
Thy will be done! It is Thy heart's desire
For all Thine own. O may we never tire
Daily therein to find our souls' delight,
As we pursue our path through this dark night.
Thy will be done! Thy holy will, so blest;
Surely for us 'tis Thine own path of rest,
To follow Thee and bear Thy yoke in love,
Till called by Thee to yon blest realms above.
Thy will be done; we'd wholly live to Thee,
Till God shall call us home with Thee to be;
Ever to dwell in love unmeasured, deep,
We who are watching now, and they who sleep.
Lord Jesus Christ, our Saviour Thou,
We know Thou hast redeemed us
We know the love that brought Thee down,
Down from that bliss on high;
To give Thyself, Thine all, for us,
Our Saviour Jesus - Lord Thou art,
Eternal too our songs of praise
E'en now we praise the grace divine,
The love that shines in Thee;
The rich one Thou - for us made poor,
By death to set us free.
O what a theme of praise art Thou,
Thy cross, Thy work, Thy word!
We ne'er shall fathom all Thy love,
"Come unto Me - and I will give you rest";
What blessed words to weary ones addressed!
They come from Him who knew the depth of woe,
And felt for sinners as none here below.
"Come unto me," yes, come in all your sin!
Through Jesus' blood the vile may enter in,
May come to God who knows their guilt and need,
Assured the blood was shed for them indeed.
"Come unto me," yes, God Himself says, Come!
He sees afar, and runs to welcome home
Unworthy sinners, who have nought to plead
But God's own love and their exceeding need.
"Come unto me," O blessed open door!
For those who but for Christ had hoped no more;
O love of God! told out in full extent,
When Jesus to those depths of darkness went.
Hast thou heard God's wondrous message,
In His call of love to Thee?
Wouldst Thou turn from such entreaty,
Once, yea twice, He may have spoken,
As He waits Thy heart to win;
Waits to fill thy soul with gladness,
Free thee from thy load of sin.
Now He calls again - O hearken!
He may never call thee more;
Wilt Thou, canst thou spurn the message,
Turn thee now to Him, repenting;
Lord, to our souls Thy light is ever pure,
And brings from heav'n what Thou alone canst give;
Yea, brings Thyself, the revelation sure
Of heav'n's eternal bliss: in Thee we live!
We bless Thee, Lord! Of Thee our song shall speak -
Poor and unworthy strains, yet still of Thee.
Come, fill our souls! This blessing would we seek,
To dwell in love, and God our dwelling be.
Be Thou with us! Let no distracting thought
Intrude to hide from us that heav'nly light.
Be Thou our strength! Let not what Thou hast brought
Be chased by idle nature's poor delight.
Be Thou our all! Thy love can fill the soul -
That love that soars beyond all creature thought;
In spirit bring where endless praises roll,
And fill our longing hearts till there we're brought.
Our God, for ever may Thy Name be blest,
For Thou dost give us now to share Thy rest.
To head up all in One was Thy great thought,
And dwell with those in whom Thy grace has wrought.
Love flows unhindered and our hearts are free;
Fresh notes of praise arise in song to Thee;
And strains of worship that shall never end,
As fragrant incense to Thyself ascend.
Thy glory bright, Thy majesty divine,
Resplendent in the face of Jesus shine.
Before Thee bowed, with joy our souls adore,
And give Thee praise and blessing evermore.
The sovereign, changeless, living God, art Thou;
Thy radiant glory rests upon us now.
Revealed in Christ Thy wondrous plan we see,
That Thou for ever all in all shouldst be.
O Lamb of God, still keep us
With foes and snares around us,
The grace that sought and found us
In all their cares and woe.
Soon shall our eyes behold Thee
We'll sing Thy power and grace;
How ready e'en now is our God to impart
Rich blessings, unmeasured, conceived in His heart!
For Christ has once suffered for sins to atone,
His shed blood upholding the claims of God's throne.
Glad tidings of pardon and peace now are heard,
As freely proclaimed by God in His word.
The way of repentance and faith now is shown
That riches in glory in Christ may be known.
And we, through the gift of the Spirit, may know
The secret of power and joy here below.
Thus freed from the world and its claims we can raise
Our satisfied hearts to outpour in His praise.
Our God, from Thee in love divine
Greatness and power and glory shine,
Head over all, Thy Name we praise,
With willing hearts our voices raise,
In spirit and in truth we sing;
To Thee, O God, our worship bring,
And, in the shining of Thy face,
We know in Christ our joyous place,
The city shines with precious light,
As bride adorned in glory bright,
And Thou, who makest all things new,
Thou art, O Lord, the centre
Of that vast world of bliss,
Where nought of sin can enter,
There Thou dost all things fill;
For Thou art Head, who suff'redst
Thou hast, O Lord, Thy seat;
Thou art the Head of all things,
Thou art our Head in glory,
In Thee our place we see;
And to Thee a note we raise:
Thou art with us in the service,
And art in us as we praise.
By Thy presence moved in spirit,
We have access to the Father,
Held by Christ in that blest place.
Blest Spirit, we would sing to Thee,
Thou source of life and liberty;
Springs of refreshing we have known,
Sent here from heav'n; Thy grace we own,
In Godhead glory Thou art one
With both the Father and the Son,
Within our hearts the love of God;
Among the many led by Thee
We find our part in liberty,
Marked as the sons of God.
Great God of wonders! all Thy ways
But the blest triumphs of Thy grace -
Who is a pardoning God like Thee?
Or who has grace so rich and free?
With wonder filled, and holy joy
We hail the pardon of our God;
Pardon for sins of deepest dye,
A pardon traced in Jesus' blood.
To pardon thus is Thine alone;
Mercy and grace are both Thine own.
Soon shall this strange, this wondrous grace,
Fill the wide earth, while sweeter praise
Sounds its own note in heav'n above.
Who is a pardoning God like Thee?
Or who has grace so rich, so free?
Thy death, O Lord, and sorrow
In that great stoop of Thine.
Thy path of love we treasure;
And though Thou art in glory,
thy love is still the same
As when its depth and fulness
thy love o'er all has triumphed,
The power of death has witnessed
"Thou art the Same," our one, unchanging God,
Who sittest high above the angry flood;
With Thee for refuge, and with Thee for strength,
We shall, though fierce the storm, reach home at length.
If on the road we find a vale of tears,
A scene of sorrow and disturbing fears,
'Tis joy to know the time cannot be long
Ere all is changed, and sadness turn to song.
We must give thanks, though deep the sorrow here,
For 'tis in grief that Thou dost draw so near;
Dost touch Thy people in Thine own sweet way,
And turn their night of weeping into day.
O what a God! How can we sing Thy praise?
The hymn's too great for our poor hearts to raise.
And yet we must our adoration bring;
Thy Spirit lifts us up, and makes us sing.
O God of grace, our Father,
In love, which sought and found us,
And brought us nigh to Thee,
And won the rest of glory,
Chose us in Christ the Son,
That we might now the nearness
And, graced in all His fulness,
Soon all Thine own shall be
In love and joy with Thee.
Soon shall we chant Thy glory
Hark! the voice of Jesus calling,
Come, ye laden, come to Me;
I have rest and peace to offer,
Rest, thou labouring one, for thee.
Yes, though high in heav'nly glory,
Still the Saviour calls to thee;
Faith can hear His gracious accents -
Come, ye laden, come to Me!
Life is found alone in Jesus,
'Tis the gift of God sent free.
Soon that voice will cease its calling;
Now it speaks, and speaks to thee;
Wilt thou heed the gracious message,
To the Lord for refuge flee?
To Thee, Lord, for ever be!
Now with joy we worship Thee.
Lord of hosts, Thou King of glory,
Soon Thy greatness all shall own.
In Thee dwells all Godhead fulness,
On the right hand of the Greatness
Thy high seat by none is shared.
Thou dost find e'en now Thy place
O Lord, Thy face was set,
Till God's full claims should yet
Drink deep that cup of woe,
All from Thee then did flee,
God hid His face from thee,
Has sought in man to find,
Jesus, Lord, Thy grace has called us
Thou with living bread dost feed us;
Thou our Lord and Teacher art.
Lord and Christ we gladly own Thee,
Good and faithful Shepherd, keep us,
May our hearts respond to Thee;
Grant us, Lord, Thy face to see.
And shall we see Thy face,
Well known to us in present grace?
And, spotless in that heav'nly light,
No cloud, no distance, e'er shall hide
For ever we shall with Thee prove
And we love Thee, blest Lord,
Thy sorrow and Thy cross record
What makes us know Thee near.
We wait to see Thee, Lord;
Thou dwell'st in love that doth afford
Yet still we wait for Thee,
To see thee as Thou art;
Be with Thee, like Thee, Lord, and free
To love with all our heart.
Our God is light: and though we go
At every step afresh we prove
Thou weariest not, most gracious Lord,
Thou giv'st our hearts to know.
Death's bitter waters met our thirst,
But Thou didst make them sweet;
Then on our gladdened vision burst
The manna and the springing well
And Eshcol's grapes the story tell
Of where Thy path doth lead.
When I survey the wondrous cross
On which the Lord of glory died,
My richest gain I count but loss,
And pour contempt on all my pride.
Far be the thought that I should boast,
Save in the cross of Christ, my Lord;
All the vain things that charm me most,
I'd sacrifice them at His word.
There from His head, His hands, His feet,
Sorrow and love flowed mingled down;
Did e'er such love and sorrow meet,
Or thorns compose so rich a crown?
Were the whole realm of nature mine,
That were an off'ring far too small;
Demands my soul, my life, my all!
How wondrous a Saviour is God's blessed Son!
How great and eternal the work He has done!
God's glory maintained by His death on the tree,
While mercy flows freely to you and to me.
How free is the pardon His blood has procured!
How blessed the welcome His Name has ensured
To all who confess Him their Saviour and Lord -
Now brought into favour, believing His word.
On Calvary see Him who died in our stead,
In glory behold Him exalted as Head;
God's wrath He endured on Calvary's tree,
By weakness and dying the Victor was He.
To those who obey Him has God freely giv'n
The blest Holy Spirit as poured out from heav'n;
Who witnesses here to Christ's glory above:
Receiving this blessing we live in God's love.
As Son of man, of all the theme!
Come, Lord, to reign o'er all supreme,
The Man of patience waiting now,
The Man of joy, for ever, Thou:
And every tongue to Thee confess,
The Lord of all come forth to bless:
Yea, Lord, Thy word from that bright home
Is, Surely, I will quickly come!
All men have sinned and short of glory come;
The Scripture saith, None righteous, no not one!
No hope hath man, deceived and far from God,
Guilty and lost, exposed to judgment's rod.
One Mediator, Christ, of God and men,
Who on the tree once died, and rose again:
No other name but His can sinners save -
Jesus, who rose triumphant o'er the grave.
Forgiveness now is preached through Him who died,
The Lord of glory who was crucified.
His finished work has met our every need;
And brought us nigh to God as free indeed!
Sealed by the Spirit till redemption's day,
Sealed till the Bridegroom takes His bride away,
We Christ await: He will not reign alone,
But take the church, His bride, to share His throne.
Have you not heard the joyful sound?
Glad tidings through the world resound -
Who died for such as we.
Thy footsteps haste! the day draws near
When careless souls shall quake and fear.
Here is a refuge open wide,
Salvation now in Him who died.
O why not then in Christ confide?
If works could save, would He have died?
Now hearken to His blessed cry,
"'Tis finished!" He is crowned on high.
Henceforth art thou for glory meet,
By blood made nigh, in Christ complete;
And thus to walk before His face,
Blessed in the riches of His grace;
God and Father, we adore Thee,
Now revealed in Christ the Son,
Through the work that He has done.
Filled with praise we bow before Thee;
With adoring hearts we bless Thee,
In Thy wondrous love we see.
In the person of the Son,
By the Spirit we behold Him,
Object of Thy heart's deep love;
In that scene of joy above.
In Thy grace Thou now hast brought us
Sharers of Thy joy to be
And to know the blessed secret
Saviour, we long to follow Thee,
To count all else, whate'er it be,
We are not now our own, but Thine,
And made, by grace and love divine,
The sons and heirs of God.
Thy Spirit, too, the present seal
Dwells in us now and doth reveal
Thy life is now beyond the grave;
Our souls Thou hast set free;
Life, strength and grace in thee we have,
And we are one with Thee.
O teach us so Thy power to know,
That we may own, while here below,
Jesus! the very thought of Thee
But sweeter far Thy face to see
No voice can sing, no heart can frame,
A sweeter sound than Thy blest Name,
O hope of every contrite heart,
O joy of all the meek,
To those who ask how kind Thou art,
How good to those who seek!
But what to those who find? Ah! this
Nor tongue nor pen can show;
The love of Jesus, what it is,
None but His loved ones know.
Jesus! our present joy art Thou,
As Thou our prize wilt be;
In Thee be all our glory now,
Lord Jesus Christ, to thee a song we raise,
Both heart and voice uniting in Thy praise.
Thine excellence and glory fill our sight;
To Thee be honour, majesty and might!
What love from Thee to Thine assembly flows!
What nearness sweet and full she ever knows!
Her joy complete in knowing that Thy heart
Is satisfied in Thy blest counterpart.
Bone of Thy bones, flesh of Thy flesh, the bride
Can take her place in glory at Thy side,
In love's complacency - no distance known -
To her Thou'rt Head o'er all things, glorious One!
Jesus, my Saviour! Thou art mine,
The Father's gift of love divine;
What Thou hast done, and what Thou art,
Are now the portion of my heart.
Poor, feeble, failing, as I am,
I now can glory in Thy Name;
Now cleansed by thy most precious blood,
And counted righteous by Thy God.
Thy fulness, Lord, is now for me,
All my fresh springs are hid in Thee;
In Thee I live; while I confess
I nothing am, yet all possess.
O Saviour, teach me to abide
Close sheltered at Thy trusted side,
Each hour receiving grace on grace,
Until I see Thee face to face.
God gave His Son for sinners;
My soul is filled with wonder
As now His grace I see!
Shout, shout aloud, ye saved ones,
Washed in His blood most precious,
Lift up your hearts in praise
Now, all ye heirs of glory,
Shout, shout aloud, ye saved ones,
As in Thy presence, Lord, our spirits free,
Thy brethren now respond with joy to Thee;
We answer to Thy call in kinship's place,
And near to Thee we know Thine own embrace.
"My brethren" - Lord, these precious words are Thine.
What glorious thoughts now flow in light divine,
As, in this nearness, yielding Thee Thy joy,
We raise our song to Thee - our blest employ!
We praise Thee, blessed Lord; our souls would move
With joy to answer to Thy precious love.
We taste of heav'nly joys with Thee - how blest!
Thine own heart satisfied, and ours at rest.
"Not of the world" - blest words of Christ the Lord
To those who here attended on His word!
They call to us, amid our pilgrim ways,
And draw us, Father, to Thy world of praise.
Out of the world to Thine own blest abode
We follow our Forerunner to His God.
As, bought by blood, we do not here belong -
"Not of the world" becomes our joyful song.
"Not of the world", O words of deep delight!
What rest and strength their heav'nly tones incite!
May we be worthy, Father, of such love!
O teach us all, who have this glorious lot,
To seek for nothing where our Lord is not.
Be this our song, our glory and our plea:
"Not of the world" - our springs are all in Thee.
Blest Spirit, now we worship Thee;
Thou art in us the power
To know Christ's love and serve Him thus,
And Thou art God, Thou Holy One;
Thou art Thyself the bond between
More blessed still, the bond between
What rich eternal bursts of praise
Shall fill yon courts through endless days,
When time shall cease to be!
Round and around the notes shall swell,
As each redeemed one joins to tell
Thy love, so vast and free.
Each shall the Saviour's likeness bear,
A royal crown each brow shall wear,
To Thee, O Lamb of God, to thee,
Our joy unhindered then with Thee,
Our eyes undimmed Thy glory see,
As we await that cloudless day,
Our burning hearts with rapture say
He died that we might live!
The joy of earth and heav'n;
In which the sons of men can boast,
Than His who seeks and saves the lost.
And is from guilt set free;
His heart o'erflows with sacred joy,
And songs of praise his lips employ.
But soon, to give Thee worthy praise,
Both heav'n and earth their songs shall raise.
Our hearts Thou dost console, O Lord,
Thy Spirit speaks to us Thy word,
And dwells with us throughout the night.
Thy voice, O Lord, is near at hand;
The Spirit gives us access free;
He helps us here to understand,
And moves our hearts with thoughts of Thee.
The memory of Thy wondrous love
Thine own still treasure here below;
While in this waste, from heav'n above
Thy glory and Thy grace we know.
Thine is the world of life, where more
By far than Eshcol's grapes is found:
Refreshment, strength, from Thy vast store
We have, despite the barren ground.
But soon the Spirit's gentle grace
And we in light, and face to face -
Thou Holy One - shall speak to Thee.
Lord Jesus, holy lamb of God,
Who shed'st for us Thine own life-blood,
Come, teach us all Thy love - then pain
In life were sweet, and death were gain.
Take Thou our hearts, and let them be
For ever held, O Lord, for Thee.
Thy willing servants, let us wear
The seal of love for ever there.
How blest are they who still abide
Close sheltered by Thy watchful side,
Who life and strength from Thee receive,
And with Thee move, and in Thee live!
Ah, Lord, enlarge our scanty thought,
To know the wonders Thou hast wrought;
Unloose our stamm'ring tongues to tell
I love to sing of Jesus,
To me most sweet and precious,
Of Him who came to die!
Yes, then the work He finished,
My sins all laid upon Him,
And now the Lord is risen,
The love of God to know.
To live e'en now to God
And soon He's coming for me,
Where still I'll sing the story
Lo! He comes, from heav'n descending,
Swell the triumph of His train.
Jesus comes, and comes to reign.
And His saints, by man rejected,
See the Son of God appear!
Israel's race shall then behold Him,
Though they set at nought and sold Him,
Pierced and nailed Him to the tree,
Lord, the bride is with the Spirit
Calling on Thee now to come;
And to sit upon Thy throne.
Travails, groans, till Thou shalt come.
Yea! Amen! let all adore Thee,
Saviour, take the power and glory,
All the nations God has giv'n.
To Thee both heart and voice we raise:
To Thee be honour, power and praise.
The whole vast scene of glory bright,
What mind sublime could this conceive!
What power divine could all achieve!
With wonder filled, sustained and blest,
The many sons who share Thy rest
God all in all, we worship Thee,
Thy grace, O Lord, that measured once the deep
Of Calv'ry's woe, to seek and save Thy sheep,
Has touched our hearts and made them long for Thee,
Thyself our treasure and our all to be.
Thy glory, Lord, at God's right hand above,
Supreme of all in that blest scene of love,
In sonship tells our hearts their wondrous place,
In Thee accepted by the Father's grace.
Thy beauties, Lord, Thy holy precious worth,
Surpassing far the deepest joys of earth,
Attract our hearts - our joy Thy constant love,
Thyself our object in those scenes above.
Thy fulness, Lord, of light and love divine,
No thought can grasp, nor human mind define.
The whole vast scene of glory will display
That fulness in a quickly-coming day.
When all things filled by Thee are wholly blest,
And God's deep love eternally shall rest
In that which ever speaks to Him of Thee,
Thy greatness, Lord, the universe shall see.
Jesus, our Lord, the mighty power
Has brought us to this holy hour,
Thy church in Thine embrace shall be
Yielded in blest response is she,
Thou dost fill all in this blest sphere
Where we are at Thy side;
With Thee, Thy fulness, brought so near,
And O how blest! that place above
As purposed in the Father's love
His joy and Thine to be.
Thou, in Thine own blessed service
Telling her of all His glory,
And we worship Thee, blest Spirit,
Blest Son of God, Thou holy One above,
In whom both love and light with truth combine;
Seated and crowned in yonder world of love,
In Thy blest face we see God's glory shine.
We bless Thee for the love which brought Thee down
From Godhead glory to the cross of woe!
Thou who on earth as Man didst win renown,
For Thou by death didst Satan's power lay low.
Thy cross, blest Lord! what unsearched depths of love
Are told, when God's sharp judgment-sword awoke!
And, darkness all around, from Him above
On Thee, O Saviour, fell the dreadful stroke!
Whose glory claimed Thee from the gloomy grave!
Exalted we behold Thee at His side,
The crowned Victor, mighty now to save.
In this blest and sacred hour,
Yield we worship, praise and blessing,
Thou art God through all the ages,
Sons, the fruit of holy counsel,
Praise Thy great and glorious Name.
Blessed God, Thou Head of all things,
All Thy path of sorrow here,
And those closing scenes of anguish
Deep Thy sorrow then, Lord Jesus,
Deeper far than thought can reach;
Far beyond all tongues to teach.
None could follow there, blest Saviour,
When Thou didst for sins atone;
Thou didst measure then sin's distance,
Darkness, wrath and curse were Thine;
Thus we learn Thy love divine!
What will it be with God to dwell,
And there to gaze on Jesus' face!
To meet the One we've known so well
As Priest and Saviour - in that place!
Before Christ's judgment seat to stand,
With Him look back on all the way;
To learn the meaning, at His hand,
Of every deed in every day!
Clearer than ever shall we see
The grace which God our Saviour showed,
The love that led so faithfully
How blessed when this time is o'er,
To find that love had all-sufficed,
As there upon the heav'nly shore
We reach the day of Jesus Christ!
Spirit of God, to Thee we bow in praise,
For Thou art God, the ever holy One:
One with the Father and the Son, Thy ways
Are merged with Theirs in all that has been done.
Thou didst Thyself, in feelings all sublime,
To hover o'er the scene of waste come down,
Before God made the vast expanse in time,
To work out all His great designs in man.
And when at length the Son on earth did stand,
Thou didst descend in love to mark Him out;
Thenceforth to be the power of His hand,
E'en to the off'ring of Himself to God.
And now in lowlier stoop and tireless love,
Thou from th'ascended Christ to us hast come,
To open to our view the things above,
And guide and lead a heav'nly people home.
A longing now to yield Thee
This joy Thou long hast waited,
All fair art Thou, Lord Jesus,
Now held in nearness to Thee,
As Man Thou hast a bride,
One with Thee now in glory,
Gazing on thee, Lord, in glory,
While our hearts in worship bow,
There we read the wondrous story
Of the cross, its shame and woe.
All the depths of Thy heart's sorrow
Where no pitying eye was found;
Now to God's right hand exalted,
With Thy praise the heav'ns resound.
Did Thy God e'en then forsake Thee,
Hide His face from Thy deep need!
In Thy face, once marred and smitten,
All His glory now we read.
Gazing on it we adore Thee,
Thou, the Lamb, art ever worthy!
This be earth's and heav'n's accord.
O what a debt we owe
To Him who shed His blood,
And cleansed our souls, and gave us power
For we can call Thy God, our God,
Who gave with Thee the Spirit's cry
Who dwelt in light supremely bright,
But stooped to tell the story
In hearts which now adore Thee.
But take in grace a bondman's place,
To Calv'ry's death Thy blessed feet
Thy Father's will Thou wouldst fulfil,
O Lord, we raise our song of praise,
We wait the day when Thy blest sway
Shall fill the earth with blessing;
God our Father, we Thy children
Seek Thy help this favoured hour;
God and Father, bless us now,
As before Thy throne we bow.
Here we meet and wait before thee,
Finding in our hearts a place.
God our Father, bless us now,
As before Thy face we bow.
We own Thee Lord and Teacher,
May we, as in the temple,
Of truth which sets us free.
Lord, by Thy Spirit teach us
That through Thee now in all things
God moves in a mysterious way
He plants His footsteps in the sea,
He treasures up His bright designs,
Ye fearful saints, fresh courage take,
The clouds ye so much dread
Are big with mercy, and shall break
The bud may have a bitter taste,
But sweet will be the flower.
Blind unbelief is sure to err,
And scan His work in vain;
And he will make it plain.
In heav'n more sweet and loud:
To Him who cleansed our sins
To Him, we sing in joyful strain,
Be honour, power and praise, Amen.
His was the shame and loss,
The might work was all His own,
Though we shall share His glorious throne.
O God, Thy glory shines supreme;
Great source of life, Thy wondrous works
Thy ways, how just and wise and true,
We bless Thee for Thy matchless grace
More blessed still, Thy heart made known
In Him who came to die,
In Jesus Christ Thy Son, who lives
Thy counsel planned in ages past
Before Thy face with Him we stand,
Our God, to Thee all glory be,
With hearts at rest in Thine own love,
Our song to Thee we raise.
Blest Father, in Thy wondrous grace
To be before Thee with Thy Son,
Clothed in the worth of that blest One
To bring to pass Thy counsels wise,
As Man He came to die,
Thine answer to His suffering love,
Christ now in glory is above,
O Father, how we love to raise
Thyself in all Thy fulness blest,
Our hearts well forth in praise.
We worship Thee, blest father Thou,
Thy glory fills our willing hearts,
Jesus, our Lord, on the throne of the Father Thou'rt crowned;
Thou once on Calvary suff'redst, of man the disowned;
We Thy beloved, remember Thee, Lord, and Thy dying;
Unto that death, as assembled, our hearts are replying;
We on Thy love are relying.
Here upon earth, till Thy coming, Thy death we are showing;
But unto Thee in the glory our hearts are outgoing;
How great, O God, our portion in Thy love,
And with Thy Christ in Thine own realms above,
Before Thyself - our God - in perfect rest,
In Thine eternal presence ever blest!
O wondrous thought of Thine, that we should be
At home, O God, in all that suiteth Thee!
Where all is of and for Thyself alone,
And finds its glorious centre in Thy Son.
'Tis by the Father's gift that we are His,
That we may be with Him and where He is,
In whom Thou dost Thy precious thoughts unfold,
As in Himself Thy glory we behold.
Beholding it, we worship and adore!
The more we learn Thy love, we love the more!
"Thou art that God," adoring hearts exclaim,
And glory gladly render to Thy Name.
Worthy art Thou to be adored!
So perfect in Thy matchless grace,
So spotless, pure in all Thy ways!
In Thee all human graces blend,
And to Thy Father did ascend
Fragrant to Him Thou ever art,
Source of rejoicing to His heart,
Fairer than all the sons of men,
Beyond all praise of tongue or pen,
Our hearts well forth in praise to Thee,
O God and Father, we our praises bring,
For who more worthy of our praise could be
Than Thou, who seekest worshippers who sing
In spirit and in truth adoringly!
All worlds Thou hast created by the Son,
All things are held by His unmeasured power;
Yet we approach Thee in that glorious One:
What cause for worship in this holy hour!
'Tis He who leads us in this blessed sphere,
And sings in the assembly unto Thee;
What joy to Him that we should thus be near
As suited and in perfect liberty!
Here we unite, our song of joy is one!
And Thou, O God, art fully satisfied.
Amidst the praises led by Christ, Thy Son,
Thou hast a dwelling ever to abide.
Now, as looking on Thy glory,
We Thy stoop in manhood trace;
And, transformed as thus before Thee,
See Thee in the Firstborn's place:
Of Thee, like Thee, for Thee, Lord!
We taste the sweetness of Thy love
And bless the love that marks Him out,
We hear His blest voice say,
And know that we are loved as He,
Our willing lips yield Thee the praise
O Lord, the bright and blessed hope,
That's cheered us through the past,
Of full eternal rest with Thee,
We'll see Thee then without a cloud -
Past conflict then: O Lord 'tis ours
To sing our song of vict'ry there,
For us, O Lord, Thou camest from on high,
And from the manger to the cross didst go;
Through suff'ring Thou didst win the victory,
And on the tree Thou barest all our woe.
From Thy heart's object turned Thee not away;
Grief, e'en to death, upon Thy spirit rolled:
Thou chosest still, blest Saviour, to obey.
Thy life laid down, our sorrows Thou didst bear,
A priceless off'ring all our thoughts above!
Thou gav'st Thyself in grace beyond compare,
Reserving nothing save the right to love.
But joy now reigns, Thy suff'rings all are o'er;
Lord, Thou art ris'n, enthroned in glory bright;
And Thy redeemed ones know for evermore
Thy peace and love, unchanging, infinite!
Unquenched by death, eternal, still the same,
Living and ever precious is Thy love!
Soon Thou shalt come Thy ransomed saints to claim,
To be with Thee for evermore above.
Blessed God, we own Thy greatness
Yet brought nigh, in holy splendour,
Of Thine own we give to Thee;
Head o'er all - how vast Thy glory -
As Thy Name so is Thy praise.
Father of lights, to Thee our hearts we lift
In thanks for every good and perfect gift;
Thou lovest still - as we approach Thy throne -
Our prayers to answer, and to bless Thine own.
Father of mercies, Thou from day to day
Dost comfort and sustain us on our way;
We praise Thee that Thou givest us below,
The depth and fulness of Thy love to know.
O Holy Father, may Thy Name be blest!
Thy chosen ones in Thee may safely rest,
Since by Thy power and with Thy presence near,
Kept in Christ Jesus, they have nought to fear.
Father of glory, who art ever wise,
How wondrous are Thy counsels in our eyes!
How vast the heritage that Thou dost see
For ever in the saints secured for Thee!
Father, we thank Thee and we bless Thy Name;
To Thee we voice our praise with one acclaim;
Thy love and grace, surpassing every need,
The deepest longings of our hearts exceed.
Wilt Thou yield to love's entreaty?
From the God who marks Thy goings
Dost Thou feel that Thou hast wandered,
From sin's burden He would free Thee,
And with love's embrace receive thee,
Grace has met the claims of justice
When thy journey all is over,
Shalt for ever be a trophy
These words evoke and answering chord;
We see Thee on the path below,
That led the way to Calv'ry's woe.
A King, despite a crown of thorn!
Despised, O Lord, and left alone,
The guilt of many Thou didst bear;
Blest answer to the sinner's need!
O holy Saviour, Thou didst die,
And for us in the grave didst lie!
But now in triumph Thou art gone
To sit upon the Father's throne.
Our voices now we gladly raise;
In one loud anthem we combine
To celebrate such love as Thine!
And meekly bowed His blessed head,
Poured out His soul, and died.
The veil by God was rent in twain,
And He who died now lives again:
In that blest word. No angel knows
Love far beyond all angel ken,
The work of Christ in love for men,
No other hand need aught to bring,
Are thus for Him made fit.
O come to the Saviour, He's calling today;
How long wilt thou linger? His voice now obey.
He's speaking from heaven in love to thy soul;
His blood He has given; wilt thou be made whole?
The Father is calling; His language is, Come!
His rich grace is bringing the wanderers home;
His heart is delighting the lost ones to bless;
His love is inviting the weary to rest.
No need now to labour, the work has been done;
To be in God's favour, believe on the Son!
Christ's death has secured salvation so free;
The cross He endured for you and for me.
The Saviour is coming for all who believe,
From heaven descending His own to receive.
O sinner, confess Him, the throne-seated Lord;
And thou shalt be with Him where He is adored.
Lord, it has touched our hearts that Thou
A rich occasion, Thee to know,
Thy grace, O Lord, has furnished now
As gathered to Thy precious Name,
We bless Thee for this hour.
The love that gave Thyself for us
Its fresh appeal - a joy to those
To Thee, O God, we raise!
For Thou art Head o'er all;
Thou art the God of glory,
We praise Thee in Thy splendour,
For all things are of Thee,
Through Thee, O God, and for Thee,
Our hearts delight in Christ, and long
Of Thee we make our loftier song,
We cannot from Thy praise forbear.
Our ready tongues make haste to sing
The glories of the heav'nly King.
Fairer than all the earth -born race,
Replenished are Thy lips with grace,
And full of love Thy tender heart.
God ever blest! we bow the knee,
And own all fulness dwells in Thee.
Be Thou the object bright and fair
To fill and satisfy the heart;
Our hope to meet thee in the air,
And nevermore from Thee to part;
To follow, serve, and wait for Thee.
Well may we sing, with triumph sing,
The glories of the living God,
The love of God it was that sought
From sin to set us free;
That gave the Son, whose precious blood
In Him we read the Father's love,
We meet in Him a Saviour God,
Then gladly sing and sound abroad
The glories of the living God,
Father, from our hearts is springing,
Praise which He, the Son, is leading
To Thyself in this blest hour.
What a joy to call Thee Father,
Blest indeed as with Thy Son,
And to know Thy love in nearness,
Fruit of triumphs He has won.
Great the cost to Thee, blest Father,
For Thou didst not spare Thy Son,
Answered now in those who worship
In the good of what He's done.
So to Thee, supreme in all things,
As we greet Thee in Thy rest.
It is to Thee our voices now we raise,
Blest Spirit of adoption; Thee we praise,
As, in the light of sonship's glorious place,
We serve by Thee before the Father's face.
Thy blessed, holy Person be adored
By those whose hearts respond with one accord;
For Thou hast served that we, through boundless grace,
Might know with Christ a son's eternal place.
Access by Thee, through Christ, in that blest sphere -
We know and prove the love which casts out fear;
And, restful in God's grace as now brought nigh,
We joy with Thee, and "Abba, Father!" cry.
Both Lord and Christ is made.
In love He came from heaven,
He paid in full the price;
By Him who came to die.
Our God and Father, we are here to share
True is our love and genuine our care
As moved by Christ's own feelings in our heart,
We long to bear with priestly hands our part.
The sanctity of Thine abode on earth
That by unholy ways its holy worth
The couch of Solomon we would surround
With valiant love and reverence profound.
Blest Spirit, who art here in charge of all
On Thee, our Paraclete, we humbly call
Hold us in faith, in dignity and power,
Throughout this privileged and sacred hour.
In light unclouded dwells the mighty God,
His glory all creation doth proclaim;
A Spirit - love and light, the Holy One -
Who is, who was, who is to come, the Same!
The only glorious, the eternal God,
Who ever lived before beginnings were!
The glory of the One who set them there!
The Triune God, almighty, yet unseen;
The ever holy, holy, holy One
Whose word existence to creation gave,
What joy it is to contemplate Thyself
In Christ revealed, the everlasting God!
To learn Thy wisdom, search Thy matchless grace;
To worship Thee, as saints redeemed by blood!
To see Thy glory in the face of Christ,
And without let enjoy - in heav'n above,
In realms of cloudless light and joy and peace -
Thine own unending, changeless, perfect love!
Lord, Thy ways are past our searching,
Thou dost break earth's links asunder,
To Thyself our souls dost bind.
By the cords of love Thou drawest
Each blest object of Thy grace;
Thou wilt daily keep us near Thee,
Till in heav'n we see Thy face.
None shall mar our joy in Thee!
Soon will change earth's toil and sorrow
We would trust Thee without seeing,
Knowing that Thy way is best;
Dark or bright, in Thee confiding,
Shall our hearts find peace and rest.
Blest God and Father, source of joy
For all Thine own in sonship's place,
Our songs of praise arise to Thee -
We worship now before Thy face.
Thy Spirit doth our hearts sustain,
As we through Christ are near to Thee;
Thy holy love fills every heart,
And in Thy presence blest are we.
Thou in Thy wondrous love hast planned
That we with Christ should have our part,
And share that home of glory bright
With Him who fills with joy Thy heart.
O blessed home, where Thou dost dwell
In holy love and glory bright!
Near Thee, Thy love rests on us now,
And we in Christ are Thy delight.
Blest in Thy presence - glorious place -
With joy we hymn Thyself on high.
O God of love, our song we raise,
Thy lowly service does not hide
Yet pleased with us to be -
The Lord is coming; lift your heads!
Soon shall we meet Him in the air,
The Lord is coming; faith gives place
This mortal swallowed up by life
The Lord is coming; what delight
The glory of that blessed sight
Yea, Lord, Thou comest - hope how blest!
Thy call we soon shall hear;
And then in glory shall Thy bride
Lord, in Thy supper now we see
The tokens of Thy matchless love!
Not death itself could stronger be
Than those affections Thou didst prove.
Thy peace, Thy joy Thou bringest here
Our souls to bless, our hearts to cheer.
The bread and cup before us now
Are witness to a work complete,
Through darkness dread, O Lord, when Thou
The awful power of death didst meet!
We praise Thee, Lord, as now come nigh,
Thee - whom we soon shall praise on high!
Eternal King of those who reign,
To Thee be honour, might, Amen.
Thy dwelling light, Thy form unknown,
Supreme art Thou, O God, alone!
Thy grace and glory, truth and love
Now seen in Christ, all praise above.
Thee would we worship and extol,
O blessed God, soon all in all!
O blessed Saviour, is Thy love
So great, so full, so free?
Fain would we have our souls, our hearts,
We love Thee for the glorious worth
We love Thee for that shameful cross,
No greater love can man display
Than for His friends to die;
Thus faithful to Thine own wast Thou:
What love with Thine can vie?
Thou like Thy brethren wouldst become,
In flesh and blood Thou didst take part,
Through death to set us free.
As man, O Lord, it was not good
Fruit of Thy death, Thou hast secured
O Lord, we treasure in our souls
And ever shall Thy Name to us
O Lord, the knowledge of Thy love
Doth bow our hearts to Thee above;
Before Thy face we prostrate fall,
Whose wondrous glory shines for all.
We worship, praise Thee and adore,
Thy church, Thy body and Thy bride,
Espoused to Thee, a virgin chaste,
While travelling still this dreary waste -
Finds in Thyself her hope, her all!
She waits to hear her Bridegroom call.
He comes! The longed-for, glorious Lord,
Whose Name by all shall be adored!
He comes to take His bride on high,
The fruits of God's eternal plan,
Before the age of time began.
The heav'n and earth, the sea and land,
Display the pow'r of God's own hand,
And all His matchless moral ways
Redound for ever to His praise;
"Lord, what is man?" 'Tis Christ who died,
When He for sins atonement made;
Worthy is He o'er all to reign!
Thy counsels ere the world began
All centred in the Son of man;
Head of the church His destined place,
Thy glory radiant in His face.
Let every creature bend the knee!
Worthy, O Son of man, art Thou
Of every crown that decks Thy brow;
Worthy art Thou to be adored
When all shall own Thy rightful sway!
Wilt Thou come, or wilt thou linger?
Death and darkness are around thee;
Thou may'st come; the vilest sinner
Thou art welcome, for to save thee
See the blood, and hear Him speaking
And on glory's heights behold Him,
Hear Him speak the word of pardon;
And thy heart shall lose its burden,
O Lord, do Thou our souls inspire
With fervent love and deep desire,
To follow Thee, Thy Name to own,
As Thy disciples thus be known.
Thou hast Thy life for us laid down,
Laid up, for us, a righteous crown.
Should we not then devoted be,
In full committal, Lord, to Thee?
O Lord, do Thou our hearts prepare
To rise to meet Thee in the air;
Our bodies changed, our spirits free,
To dwell in glory, Lord, with Thee.
Thou wilt in triumph lead Thine own,
To take, with Thee, Thy rightful throne.
In Thee, O Lord, doth dwell.
To Thee we bow the knee -
The bread and cup, O Lord, recall
The floods their voice did raise;
Thy suff'ring love afresh would learn,
Proved on that day of days.
All question of our moral stain
Thou didst resolve when Thou didst drain
So surely, that our hearts are free
Borne in Thy heart through death's dark tide
(The travail Thine), with Thee we died,
In Thee we rise on high;
With hearts now filled with glory's light,
We tread our path through earth's dark night,
Where Thou our Lord didst die.
How good and great, O Father,
To bless Thee, God our Father,
Father, Thine own Son praised Thee,
Of heav'n and earth the Lord!
For all those coming to Him -
Are held by Him for ever,
The fruit of Thy great plan.
We share His joy before Thee
In all that Thou hast done.
But in that Man so blest,
To whom Thou'st given all things,
We hear the words of love,
And we have peace with God.
Our joy still ebbs and flows;
But peace with Him remains the same;
His love, not ours, the resting-place,
Though heav'n is now His home;
The mighty stone is rolled away,
For He has left the tomb.
We know the throne on which He sits,
We know His truth and love.
We hail Thee, Lord, our glorious Head,
To Thee our praises now would rise.
Received in glory bright up there,
Are heaped upon His Son's blest brow;
He is the mighty Victor now.
The Father's throne by Him is shared,
Whose nature He, the Son, declared;
Whose will He did, the cost how great!
Those who seek Thine aid divine,
May Thy light among us shine.
Brought to us in love by Thee,
Fill our souls with holy longing
Of His glory more to see.
As the truth Thou dost unfold;
May our hearts be more retentive,
O Lord, the joy on union,
The bride, with Thee in nearness,
Where all Thy power and greatness
At rest in Thy great love.
What will it be to dwell above,
And with Thee, Lord of glory, reign,
Since the blest knowledge of Thy love
So brightens all this dreary plain?
No heart can think, no tongue can tell,
What joy 'twill be with Thee to dwell.
When left this scene of faith and strife,
And flesh and sense deceive no more;
When we shall see Thee, Prince of life,
And all Thy works of grace explore;
What heights and depths of love divine
Will there through endless ages shine!
And God has fixed the happy day
When the last tear shall dim our eyes,
When He will wipe these tears away,
And fill our hearts with glad surprise;
To hear Thy voice and see Thy face,
And know the fulness of God's grace.
We speak of the grace of our God,
So boundless, so rich, and so free;
But what will it profit Thy soul
We speak of salvation and love,
By the Father in Jesus made known;
But, if thou wouldst live unto God,
By faith thou must make it thine own.
We speak of the Saviour's great Name,
By which God can sinners receive;
Yet still art thou lost and undone
Unless in that Name thou'lt believe.
We speak of the blood of the lamb,
Which frees from pollution and sin;
But its virtues by thee must be proved,
Or thou wilt be ever unclean.
We speak of the glory to come,
Of the heavens so bright and so fair;
But, unless thou'lt in Jesus believe,
Thou wilt not, thou canst not be there.
We give Thee praise and worship,
To know Thee with and in us
We thank Thee for Thy service,
Of truth, so rich and rare.
O teach us in Thy movements
To walk in faith with Thee;
The bride of Christ must be.
To Thee, our God, we render now
How great Thy counsels were of old
In Christ and His companion - one -
For Thou art glorified as God
Our Head, of whom are we, His like,
A blessed Man amidst His own
With joy He sings Thy praises,
And in the Spirit's power we share
We worship Thee as Head o'er all,
Most blessed is Thy sovereign will,
Is witnessed in the Saviour's blood;
'Tis in the cross of Christ we trace
God could not pass the sinner by,
Justice demands that He should die;
But in the cross of Christ we see
How God can save, yet righteous be.
The judgment fell on Jesus' head,
'Twas in His blood sin's debt was paid;
Stern justice can demand no more,
And mercy can dispense her store.
The sinner who believes is free,
Can say, the Saviour died for me;
Can point to the atoning blood
And say, This made my peace with God.
I heard the blessed story told,
How once He took a bondman's form,
I saw by faith the judgment fall,
By faith I heard His cry,
And knew for me He suffered shame,
For me He stooped to die.
I heard the blessed story told,
How He in dying met the foe
I saw Him then ascended high
I knew His vict'ry set me free,
I heard the blessed story told,
When every ransomed tongue shall swell
The praise of Him who died.
I'll see Him then by all acclaimed,
And know the fulness of His love
Is, Lord Jesus, in Thy sight;
Object of Thy love - a treasure
As the pearl of greatest value,
For her Thou didst give Thine all,
Yea, Thyself in love Thou gavest;
Now Thou dost her heart enthrall.
That Thou mightest soon present her
Thou dost nourish her and cherish,
Till, without one spot of wrinkle,
Thou shalt have Thy glorious bride,
Made by God for Thee a helpmate,
We know Thee, Lord, as risen,
The heart and mind set free
To think of all Thy glory,
As now made one with Thee.
For Thou art Head o'er all things,
With joy we sing Thy praises
We can be found at rest
That love which Thou dost show
We, of Thy flesh and bones -
O Lord, what peace and rest we find
When Thy blest face we see!
What comfort fills our longing hearts
Around us all is strife and toil,
But Thou remainest still the Same,
Lord, give us peace, we pray;
Till in that scene of cloudless peace
And praise, with one adoring heart,
The God of peace and love.
The Lord who healed the leper
No frown is on His brow.
Not all Thy sins dark story
'Twas need like thine that brought Him
The Lord who touched the leper
The Lord who cleansed the leper
His blood can cleanse the vilest,
O doubt not, He is willing,
But take Him at His word,
O our God, how great, unmeasured
Is Thy love divine and blest!
We its holy depths have treasured,
As in Christ Thy Son expressed.
Thee we worship from our heart,
Praising Thee for what Thou art.
Through the depths Thy way has led,
For Thy Son who was "the Way"
We shall worship Thee for aye!
Now, O God, our hearts are bowing,
Soon shall fill the day of God.
Jesus, our Lord, Thou lovest to be near
To loving hearts who find Thyself so dear -
The precious fruit of purpose, deep, divine,
Secured and held for this great love of Thine.
Thy bride alone, Thy cherished counterpart,
Can satisfy the longings of Thy heart;
"Thou art all fair, my love," we hear Thee say,
"Arise, my love, my fair one - come away!"
Freely we yield ourselves to Thy great love,
Responding gladly, as afresh we prove
That Thou the Bridegroom art, who hast the bride
In Thine embrace - Thine own heart satisfied.
See mercy, mercy from on high,
Descend to rebels doomed to die;
'Tis mercy free, which knows no bound;
How sweet, how pleasant is the sound!
Soon as the reign of sin began,
The light of mercy dawned on man,
When God announced the blessed news,
The woman's Seed thy head shall bruise.
Brightly it beamed on men forlorn,
When Christ, the holy Child was born;
And brighter still in splendour shone
Complete in power when He arose
And burst the bands of all His foes;
And took for us His seat on high.
I am not told to labour
But blessed truth - I know it -
Christ for my soul hath suffered,
Yes, Christ has done it all!
And if I now would seek Him -
In love He sought for me,
When far from Him I wandered
He ope'd my ears, and gave me
He sought me, and He found me,
Yes, Christ has done it all!
My soul shall then still praise Him,
Yes, Thou hast done it all!
O Lord, Thy rich, Thy boundless love
No thought can reach, no tongue declare;
O give our hearts its depth to prove,
And reign without a rival there!
From Thee, O Lord, we all receive;
Thine, wholly Thine, alone we'd live.
O Lord, how cheering is Thy way!
How blest, how gracious in our eyes!
And fear before Thy presence flies.
Lord Jesus, nothing would we see,
'Mid conflict be Thy love our peace;
In weakness be Thy love our strength;
And when the storms of life shall cease
And Thou to meet us com'st at length,
Lord Jesus, then these hearts shall be
He is risen, who has suffered;
All sin's weight for us He bore.
He is risen and He liveth
From the angel to His own;
And He's seated on the throne.
He is risen! O how precious
Was that lonely Corn of Wheat!
Once in death, but now in glory,
Thousands like Him, for Him meet.
Thus to be to His assembly
Over all things now as Head.
Our God, to Thee th'assembly's praises flow
As one with Christ her Head, with love aglow;
Blest answer to the work of love divine -
The concept and the consummation Thine!
From Thee 'mid scenes supernal doth come down
The city, of Thy workmanship the crown!
Rejoicing Him who fills her heart and Thine.
The holy city doth for Thee provide
A dwelling where Thou canst with men reside.
Now, where Thy pleasure rests complacently,
Be glory in th'assembly unto Thee!
Who would hush the heav'n-sent story
Of the Lamb who came to die? -
Down to Calv'ry's depth of woe;
Now on high we bow before Thee,
Sing Him on the Father's throne;
Sing - till, heav'n and earth surprising,
Blest Holy Spirit, let us prove
As now assembled here to serve
O grant us wise discernment now,
That we may every grace allow,
Thus may the heart of Christ our Lord
As we His glory here would guard,
Precious Name! the Name of Jesus,
Who in love to guilty sinners
Precious Name of Him the Saviour,
In His grace, for ruined sinners
Precious Name of Him who suffered
On His brow the crown of glory
Sweetest Name there is in heaven,
Father, Thy love was deepest joy
He came to earth (what blest employ!)
That we this love might know.
Thy Name by Him has been declared,
And His own place by us is shared.
The lustre of His love, in death
Then to impart the living Breath,
That we His peace might share.
He now delights with us to raise
A song of triumph and of praise.
He bringeth us to this blest place
Where we with Him can sing;
On us shines favour ne'er to dim -
The love wherewith Thou lovest Him!
Lord, though Thy saints be laid to rest,
In Thee they have a portion blest;
Thy precious blood the purchase price
To be with Thee in paradise.
What power from Thee can separate?
Not death nor life, not land nor sea,
Can come between Thy saints and Thee.
"With Christ" - how better far the lot -
Where sin and sorrow enter not!
When every tear is wiped away;
When those asleep shall wakened be
And we with them shall rise to share
That rapturous meeting in the air!
As drawn to Thy blest Name;
That Name so rich in savour
Chosen ere the world was founded,
Thine own Son, the joy of heaven,
Grace on grace so richly given,
Freely rests Thy love upon Him,
And with joy we now acclaim Him,
O Thy love! Its wondrous story
See Him dying on the tree;
See who bears the awful load!
Son of man and Son of God.
Here we have a firm foundation,
Here the refuge of the lost;
Christ, the Rock of our salvation,
His the Name of which we boast.
Lamb of God! for sinners wounded,
Who on Thee their hope have built.
Our blest God and Father, we respond to Thee
Suited, in love and holy liberty,
O wondrous thought, that many there should be
Like Christ, for Thy delight eternally!
He Thy delight, in whom we have our part,
Thy love for Him, the Object of Thy heart
His glory in Thy presence now we see,
As with Him there in love's complacency.
'Tis here He sings - what joy His heart doth find,
While many sons are stirred in heart and mind
In worship, God and Father unto Thee,
Supreme, Thou source in love's economy!
Rends the tomb to claim Thine own.
Fill with song the radiant air,
Thou didst die, but O Thy rising -
Brings to God a glorious spoil,
For ever with Thyself we find
Thy glory we with joy behold,
As one with Thee - Thy flesh and bones,
Our hearts as held by Thee
That we, O God, are Thine;
Jesus, the Lord, our night broke through
And Jesus came from heav'n above,
No more in dread of wrath,
We rest our souls on Thee.
Our hearts look up to see
In spirit dwell where we shall be
With Him, Thine heirs, in heav'n.
Soon shall we see Him there;
With them and Him in glory stand,
Blest Holy Spirit, sent from heav'n above
To this dark world where sin and death abound,
To fill our hearts with heav'nly peace and love -
Our grateful praises now to Thee resound.
Blest Spirit, come, fill Thou our hearts with grace;
Join now Thy help to all our weakness here;
Strengthen our souls as we move on apace -
Remove from us unfaithfulness and fear.
Spirit of truth, come, lead our hearts above;
Bring now to us God's thoughts for us today;
Fill us with wisdom, power, peace and love -
Shine in our hearts with Thy blest heav'nly ray.
Spirit of God, we gladly Thee would hail,
Bless Thee and praise Thee as we thus bend low;
Leading the sons of God through this dark vale
Into that scene where ceaseless praises flow.
With loyal hearts, O Lord, to Thee,
Grant that we each may faithful be
And by the Spirit from above,
Here in the diligence of love,
Now with the things that are of Thee
Do Thou our hearts, Lord Jesus, hold,
And with us have Thy way,
Our wills subdued, our minds controlled,
He, the Son, declared Thy Name;
Thee we trust in grace confiding
Now we seek that power divine,
To the secrets of Thy mind.
Midst the world of death and darkness,
Till we enter Christ's blest day!
Keep us from the world of evil,
For the land of heav'nly worth.
Help us here to represent Thee,
True and faithful to Thy calling,
In the grace of Him who died.
Jesus, Thou art coming, coming as the King,
To this world of sorrow happiness to bring;
Evil then shall vanish, wars and strife shall cease,
Thou, O mighty Victor, art the Prince of Peace.
All Thy works shall praise Thee; men both high and low,
From the least to greatest, Thee as Lord shall know;
All shall call Thee blessed, all Thy Name confess;
Jesus, Thou art worthy, Sun of righteousness!
Jesus, Priest enthroned, King of righteousness,
Thou art King of Salem, Thou art King of peace;
All Thy people call Thee, call from near and far:
Come, Thou Root of David, bright and Morning Star!
Come, Thou King triumphant; all the earth is Thine;
Show Thy mighty power, let Thy glory shine;
Come, Thou King of glory, Lord of hosts in heav'n,
Come, Lord Jesus, Saviour! Even so, Amen.
Lord, the greatness of Thy Person
Fills with joy our raptured gaze;
Thou hast come in wondrous glory,
Lord of hosts, and King of glory,
Thou hast earth and heav'ns created,
To the age of age Thy throne,
Yet to us in manhood known.
Deep our souls are stirred within us
As Thy glories thus we see;
Lord, we wait for Thine appearing;
Bright the prospect is, and cheering,
Base the wish, and vain th'endeavour,
Here on earth to find our rest;
Till we see Thy face, we never
Shall or can be fully blest;
Till Thou comest keep us steady,
At Thy call may we be ready,
On Thee, Lord, with joy to gaze;
Keep us now, and all Thy children,
Keep, O keep us, in our weakness,
May the joy of Thy salvation
May we love and serve and praise Thee
Grant Thy grace that we may conquer
Bless us, guide us, save us, keep us
O the peace for ever flowing
From God's thoughts of His own Son,
O the peace of simply knowing,
On the cross that all was done.
Peace with God - for Christ in heaven
Object is of faith to me:
Peace with God - the Lord is risen,
Peace with God - for Christ's in glory;
God is just and God is love;
O how blessed is the story,
That we're brought to God above!
We confess Thee Lord of glory,
Fruits of vict'ry Thou hast won.
Spring up, O Spirit most holy!
Move us to sing to Thee now;
Teach us with gladness, yet lowly,
Here in Thy presence to bow.
Spring up, blest Spirit, within us!
Speak to our hearts of His love
Who once descended to win us -
Spring up, O Well, in Thy glory!
Open the eyes of our heart;
Grant us full freedom before Thee,
Spring up, O Spirit most gracious!
Till as we're known we shall know.
Head over all, O God, art Thou;
Divinely blest, we bring to Thee
As now in Christ we live.
Blest Father, Son, and Spirit, Thine
Through Thy great might and wisdom
To us, O God, Thy greatness
To those who have their part
With Christ; in freedom through Thy grace,
We joy in Him before Thy face.
Would our lips delight to tell:
How the Lord of life and glory
Came in love with men to dwell.
Once He sat at Sychar's well;
Here as Man in form and fashion -
God come down with men to dwell!
As the Lamb of God He suffered
For the sins He knew so well;
On the cross Himself He offered,
That Thou mightest with Him dwell.
Come to Him! His heart so tender,
And His grace would Thee compel;
Yield to Him in full surrender,
And with Him for ever dwell!
Living water He would give thee;
To the God who gives so freely,
Who would have thee with Him dwell.
Ask then for the Spirit Holy -
He who is the springing well,
Power for life and joy within thee -
He would come with thee to dwell.
We joyful raise our songs of praise,
To Thee once slain - worthy to reign -
The curse, the grave, Thy saints to save,
And have us as Thy treasure.
We see Thee as the Victim,
The Lamb once slain, alive again,
Thy saints rejoice with heart and voice,
In all Thy joy and glory,
And long to be on high with Thee
Where all shall bow before Thee.
Rock of Ages! cleft for me,
Let me hide myself in Thee;
Let the water and the blood,
From Thy riven side which flowed,
Be of sin the double cure,
Cleansing from its guilt and power.
Not the labour of my hands
Could my zeal no respite know,
Could my tears for ever flow,
Nought for sins could e'er atone
But Thy blood, and Thine alone.
Nothing in my hand I bring,
Naked, come to Thee for dress;
Helpless, look to Thee for grace;
Foul, I to the fountain fly;
Wash me, Saviour, or I die.
Found by Thee before I sought,
From Thy fulness grace on grace;
Thou hast washed me in Thy blood,
Made me live and live to God.
Jesus, Thy head, once crowned with thorns,
Thou glorious light of courts above,
To us still manifest Thy love,
That we its depths may know.
To us Thy cross with all its shame,
With all its grace, be giv'n;
Though earth disowns Thy lowly Name,
Who suffer with Thee, Lord, below,
Then let it be our joy to know
This way of peace and love.
To us Thy cross is life and health,
Our present glory, joy and wealth,
Have met the charge that on us lay,
And taken all death's sting away.
Soon all the saints who through Thee sleep,
Th'appointment in the air will keep,
When, rising from Thy Father's throne,
Thou comest forth to claim Thine own.
Thy voice the realm of death shall burst,
The dead in Christ arising first;
And, in a moment, we who live
Together then, the church will be
Caught up to meet Thee, blessed Lord,
Where Thou shalt ever be adored.
And now in faith and hope and love,
We wait to greet Thee from above;
Each heart sustained in power and grace,
Until we see Thee face to face.
Master, we would no longer be
At home in that which hateth Thee,
But patient in Thy footsteps go,
Thy sorrow as Thy joy to know.
We would - and O confirm the power! -
With meekness meet the darkest hour,
For Thou wast scorned and crucified.
We welcome still Thy faithful word -
The cross shall meet its sure reward;
For soon must pass the little while,
Then joy shall crown Thy servant's toil.
O may our path of service be
That when our earthly course is run,
We may receive Thy word, "Well done."
God manifest in flesh, O wonder of His universe!
O wisdom all divine! that takes such blessed, lowly ways
To bring to pass its holy purposes in counsels deep,
That God may find a full response in worship and in praise.
What mutual glory, known between the Father and the Son,
Where holy love in all its secret intercourse holds sway!
The Father's bosom its own sphere, where ever dwelleth One
Who fully answers to that love throughout th'eternal day.
And by the Spirit's power the Father's love e'en now we know
Within us; with the Son, its Object, ever to abide;
And the affections of the saints well forth in ceaseless flow,
Filled in the ocean of that love, a never-ebbing tide.
Spirit of grace, O Thou whose hidden might
Sustains us day by day the whole way through,
We bless Thee for Thy service, and unite
In rend'ring now the homage that is due.
Spirit of truth, 'tis Thou who lead'st us on
Into the fulness of God's purpose here;
Thou takest heav'nly glories of the Son,
And bringest every precious feature near.
Filled with the favour Thou dost make us prove,
Spirit of life, with rev'rent hearts may we
More skilfully in service learn to move,
And for the power rely alone on Thee.
Clothe us with that humility, we pray,
That honours Thee and shows what Thou canst do;
Grant that the lustre of th'eternal day -
The day of God - shine in our hearts anew.
We its fulness, power and blessing
